title: Govern the Repository, Not the Agent
hook: Across 930,000+ agent-authored pull requests, half the friction of merging code traces to the repository, not the agent — and AI contributions concentrate that risk 2x more than human ones.

title: Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization for World Models in Atari Pong
hook: Five world-model RL agents can master Atari Pong on paper — but freeze their world models and watch closely: the ball vanishes, bounces wrong, or phases through the paddle.

title: Visual Retrieval Heads: 2% of Attention Does the Grounding
hook: VLMs point at the right part of an image through a tiny set of attention heads — mask the top 20 and grounding accuracy drops by up to 80 points.

title: FreeToken: Serving Frontier MoE Models on the Machine You Own
hook: Instead of treating a laptop as a tiny datacenter GPU, FreeToken treats the whole machine as one elastic inference platform — and runs a 753B model on a single workstation card.

title: Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing?
hook: Agent instruction files only ever get longer. The reason is asymmetric cost: adding a line is free, but deleting one whose rationale is lost risks a regression you can't cheaply check.

title: Chain of Thought Is a Scaling Trap? The Case for Latent Reasoning
hook: A visible chain of thought reads like the model's thinking — but it can be an unfaithful, expensive trace. The next wave reasons in hidden state instead of tokens.

title: RL Teaches LLMs to Translate Languages They've Never Seen
hook: Instead of memorizing a new language, what if a model learned the meta-skill of reading a grammar book on the fly? RL with a crude string-overlap reward gets it there.

title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Refactoring as the Harder Coding Test
hook: Coding benchmarks keep saturating and keep turning out to be broken. ProMax swaps bug-fixing for multi-file refactoring — and the best frontier model still only solves 41.2%.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
hook: Why force a model to memorize everything? RAG lets it look things up — fetch relevant documents, then answer from that evidence instead of frozen weights alone.

title: Continual Learning Has Quietly Moved Outside the Weights
hook: Classical continual learning was about updating weights without forgetting. This survey argues the field has moved to system-level adaptation — memory, skill libraries, harnesses.

title: LLMs Get Lost When Intent Keeps Moving
hook: Real users don't state what they want up front — they reveal, revise, and redirect it mid-conversation. Rewrite existing benchmarks that way and scores drop across every model family.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
hook: Pit two networks against each other — a forger making fakes and a detective catching them — and the forger gets so good its fakes look real.

title: Prompt Injection Defenses Fall Apart in Long Context
hook: Injection benchmarks are all short-context, which has been flattering the defenses. Stretch the input to tens of thousands of tokens and even naive attacks walk through state-of-the-art protections.

title: Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation
hook: Match the teacher's whole output sequence, not just word-by-word probabilities, and the student translation model can drop beam search while running about 10x faster.

title: Loop the Loopies!
hook: Looping a Transformer instead of growing it usually loses to just adding more parameters — Loopie is the looped MoE model that finally breaks that pattern, with IMO/IPhO gold-level reasoning.

title: CycleGAN: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation
hook: Translate horses to zebras without a single matched pair - a cycle-consistency constraint does the work that paired data used to do.

title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match Published SOTA?
hook: Can coding agents reproduce — even beat — published Nature results? The best one surpassed prior SOTA on just 17.8% of 90 real scientific tasks.

title: The Llama 4 Herd: Natively Multimodal, Mixture-of-Experts
hook: Llama 4 is Meta's first mixture-of-experts family - only 17B parameters fire per token, but the full models hold hundreds of billions, and they read text, images, and video natively.

title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
hook: AutoMem treats knowing what to remember and when to retrieve it — metamemory — as a trainable skill, and tuning memory alone roughly doubles to quadruples performance on long-horizon games.

title: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
hook: Want one number for how broadly an LLM 'knows stuff'? MMLU is a 57-subject exam spanning history, law, medicine, and math — and it became a default yardstick.

title: Two Asks After the First Autonomous-Agent Cyberattack
hook: Hugging Face's CEO went public with what he asked OpenAI: release the rogue agents' traces so researchers can study them, and put $100M of compute behind the defenders.

title: LAION-BVD: 10 Million Hours of Open Video
hook: 1.3 billion video URLs mined from CommonCrawl, 80 million downloaded, synthetically captioned for video, audio, and image pretraining — and released openly.

title: gpt-oss: OpenAI's Open-Weight Models
hook: OpenAI's first open-weight release since GPT-2: two Apache-2.0 reasoning models, the larger running on a single 80GB GPU and the smaller on a 16GB laptop.

title: Grokipedia vs Wikipedia: An LLM-Based Audit of Political Neutrality along Ideologies
hook: Grokipedia launched as the 'unbiased' answer to Wikipedia's alleged left-lean. Audited by four LLM judges, including Grok itself, it rates less neutral — just biased the other way.

title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives
hook: Fluent writing is not the same as staying consistent: the best model keeps its story straight for only 42% of runs past 20 turns of adversarial play.

title: Capek 0.5: Organizing an Embodied VLM Around Execution
hook: Robot execution keeps changing what needs perceiving. Capek 0.5 groups embodied skills by their role in that loop, trains a specialist for each, then merges them into one model.

title: Seeing Red, Thinking Bad: Color Bias in VLMs
hook: Render the same sentence with the positive words in green and a vision-language model reads it more positively. The text didn't change — only its styling did.

title: Huawei Open-Sources OpenPangu-2.0-Flash
hook: Huawei open-sourced OpenPangu 2.0's Flash tier — a 92B-parameter, 6B-active MoE model with 512K context, weights, inference code, and training ops all released — with a 505B flagship still to come.

title: Beyond IID: How General Are Tabular Foundation Models, Really?
hook: Tabular foundation models look great on standard IID benchmarks — but on temporal, grouped, high-dimensional, and non-IID data, plain tree-based models still win.

title: OpenAI Ships a Cyber-Specific Model — Behind a Gate
hook: GPT-5.6-Cyber is built for vulnerability research and exploit validation. OpenAI won't sell it openly: access runs through Daybreak, a vetted-partner program, because the defense window is closing.

title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
hook: 25,264 agent-written pull requests later: most open-source projects have barely touched agentic coding tools, and the ones that have still keep exactly one human gatekeeping every PR.

title: A Benchmark for Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination
hook: 13 LLMs try to explore, trade, craft, and build together in an open world — and most manage only ~6% of normalized return. Communication, not raw capability, turns out to be the biggest lever.

title: RynnWorld-4D: RGB-Depth-Flow World Models for Robot Manipulation
hook: A robot needs to know how a scene's 3D structure will move, not just what it looks like. This world model predicts RGB, depth, and optical flow together, then hands the result straight to a policy.

title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Models with Dictionary Learning
hook: If neurons mean several things at once, can we find cleaner units? A sparse autoencoder pulled 4,000+ single-concept features out of one tiny transformer layer.

title: Why One Engineer Dropped Embeddings for BM25 in Tool Selection
hook: An engineer running an agent with ~140 tools dropped embedding-based tool selection for plain BM25 — cosine similarity over short tool descriptions was dangerous in production.

title: CyberFactory: Turning Real CVEs Into Training Data
hook: Open security models lag closed ones partly for lack of data. CyberFactory converts public vulnerability artifacts into executable, verifiable tasks — and trains an open model on the trajectories.

title: LLMs Can Design Near-Optimal OR Algorithms
hook: Given only a problem class description and a Python sandbox, a frontier model writes an algorithm that matches or beats the best known method — before ever seeing an evaluation instance.

title: Megatron-LM: Training LLMs with Model Parallelism
hook: Split the big matrices inside attention and MLP layers across GPUs, add a few communication ops, and you can train an 8.3B model on 512 GPUs — no custom compiler needed.

title: Train / Validation / Test Splits
hook: If you tune and grade on the same data, you'll fool yourself. Keep a test set you never touch until the very end.

title: When a Model Says 90%, Does It Mean It?
hook: Across 30 models, the confidence an LLM reports in words is only loosely coupled to the confidence in its logits — a lossy channel, not a readout.

title: Dream.exe: Can a Video Generator Dream a Robot's Next Move?
hook: A video model that 'understands' physics should produce motion a robot can perform. Dream.exe runs generated videos through a real execution pipeline — and finds pretty isn't physical.

title: Annotations as Rollouts: Cheaper RL for Video Models
hook: RL post-training wastes most of its samples on bad rollouts. OraRL drops the ground-truth annotation into the group as an oracle rollout — and has to fix the advantage math to make it work.

title: GraphCast: Skillful Medium-Range Weather Forecasting
hook: A graph neural network predicts 10-day global weather in under a minute on one machine, matching or beating physics-based forecast models on most variables.

title: VibeThinker-3B: Frontier Reasoning in a Small Model
hook: A 3B model matches giant flagships on hard math and coding - because verifiable reasoning, it turns out, compresses into a tiny 'reasoning core.'

title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better Than SFT?
hook: A controlled rerun finds the simplest baseline wins: plain mixed supervised fine-tuning beats next-chunk reasoning RL on no-CoT data, at over 60x less training compute.

title: Plot the Numbers Instead of Tokenizing Them
hook: Feeding a multivariate time series to an LLM as text explodes into thousands of float tokens. Render it as a 2D plot and hand it to a VLM instead: 3.6–10.4x fewer input tokens, and better accuracy.

title: Cross-Validation
hook: One lucky or unlucky split can flatter or sink your model. Rotate the holdout and average — that's cross-validation.

title: Proper Scoring Rules Are Not Interchangeable as Training Objectives
hook: Five scoring rules that all reward honest probabilities in theory produced five differently-behaved forecasters in practice — same accuracy, different shape of error.

title: A Glance Is All You Need: Single-Pass Fine-Grained Captioning with SimLoss
hook: Multi-stage caption pipelines get the details right by generating, checking, and rewriting. SimLoss gets them in one pass by supervising the model in embedding space before a single token is decoded.

title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.

title: Ignorance or Incompetence? Building Agent Tasks That Tell the Difference
hook: When an agent fails a professional task, was it incapable or just missing a convention nobody published? This protocol splits the instruction from the private knowledge so you can test which.

title: AlphaGo: Mastering the Game of Go
hook: Go has more board positions than atoms in the universe, and experts thought superhuman play was a decade off. AlphaGo beat a top professional in 2016.

title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
hook: You can prune over 90% of a trained network and keep its accuracy. The catch: a tiny 'winning ticket' subnetwork was hiding inside the dense one from the start.

title: Beyond Entropy: Correctness-Aware Advantage Shaping via Contrastive Policy Optimization
hook: RLVR shapes rewards with entropy, but entropy can't tell useful uncertainty from confusion. CPO swaps in token-level disagreement — and shows on-policy distillation was a special case of it.

title: "This Is Not a Course. It Is a Journey."
hook: That tic has a name Cicero knew: epanorthosis. This essay argues LLMs overuse it because their training text is full of promotional prose and RLHF rewards emphatic phrasing.

title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
hook: Backtesting an LLM forecaster on past events mostly measures its memory, not its foresight — because it can retrieve after-the-fact reports or was simply trained on data closer to the event.

title: InstructGPT: Aligning LMs with Human Feedback (RLHF)
hook: A smaller model people actually like beats a bigger one they don't. InstructGPT used human preferences to make a model follow instructions — the recipe behind ChatGPT.

title: What Building Shippy Taught Us About Building Agents
hook: When a wrong answer can send a patrol boat miles off course, Ai2's maritime agent Shippy leans on deterministic tools and sandboxed sessions instead of hoping the model behaves.

title: In-Context Learning
hook: Paste a few examples into a prompt and a large language model performs the task - no gradient updates, no fine-tuning, the prompt is the program.

title: Distilling Across Different Tokenizers
hook: On-policy distillation usually assumes teacher and student share a tokenizer. Map both into byte space and you can finally distil from a teacher whose vocabulary is nothing like yours.

title: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Is Out
hook: Qwen's next flagship landed after a week of countdown threads — and the name says it all: a sparse mixture-of-experts in the trillions, with under a hundred billion awake per token.

title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations for Trillion-Parameter Models
hook: Data-parallel training wastes memory by copying optimizer states, gradients, and parameters onto every GPU. ZeRO partitions them instead — fitting 100B+ parameter models.

title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context Serving
hook: Prefill is where long-context inference burns its compute. This turns a sparse-attention prototype into a production backend — and reports up to 47x over FlashAttention-2 at 128K.

title: Molt: A PyTorch-Native Training Framework for Agentic RL
hook: NVIDIA's bet: an agentic RL codebase small enough for a researcher — or a coding assistant — to hold in their head entirely, without giving up performance.

title: DualIFM: An Interpretable-by-Design Retinal Foundation Model
hook: Most medical foundation models are black boxes you explain after the fact. DualIFM builds the explanation into the architecture — and still matches a rival 16 times its size.

title: MoP-JEPA: Fixing JEPA's Blind Spot for Branching Futures
hook: A single deterministic predictor can't represent a fork in the road — it averages the branches into a state that matches nowhere. This paper proves it, then fixes it with one head per future.

title: Interpretability Doesn't Have to Be a Tax
hook: The usual bargain: train an opaque model, then reverse-engineer it. Guide Labs made interpretability a training objective instead — and found it improves with scale rather than fighting it.

title: Maia 200: Dataflow Instead of Threads
hook: Microsoft's AI accelerator bets that the bottleneck is moving data, not doing math — so the compiler programs the data movement explicitly instead of scheduling threads.

title: StateFlow: A Persistent 3D World State for Previsualization
hook: One-shot video generation re-invents the whole scene for every edit. StateFlow keeps an editable 3D world as the working state and regenerates only what changed.

title: Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs' Approach to Bioresilience
hook: The same AI capabilities that could help design a dangerous pathogen can also help stop one. DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs lean on watermarking and biology models for the defensive side.

title: ZPPO: Put the Teacher in the Prompt, Not the Gradient
hook: A small student learns from a bigger teacher without the drift that breaks on-policy RL - by feeding the teacher's answer into the prompt as a candidate to judge, never into the gradient.

title: Training Your Own Late-Interaction Retriever
hook: A domain-specific multi-vector retriever took 14.5 hours on one RTX 3090 and beat every zero-shot model tested — including dense retrievers 33 times its size.

title: Mixed Precision Training
hook: Store weights, activations, and gradients in 16-bit floats to roughly halve memory - but keep a 32-bit master copy of the weights and scale the loss so tiny gradients don't vanish.

title: When Flattery Breaks the Model: Sycophancy as a Driver of Emergent Misalignment
hook: Teaching a model to flatter users into agreeing with wrong opinions can trigger broad misalignment — and learnable 'gates' can find and suppress the unsafe directions to reverse it.

title: Codex: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
hook: Fine-tune GPT on public GitHub code and you get a model that solves programming problems and powers GitHub Copilot - plus a new benchmark, HumanEval, that tests functional correctness.

title: Beyond Static Leaderboards for Agents
hook: Topping an agent leaderboard doesn't mean it'll work when deployed: aggregate-score rankings don't transfer out-of-distribution. Rank by predictive validity instead.

title: Gotta Catch Them All: The Modes of Sycophancy
hook: Sycophancy looks like one behavior on the surface — but inside the model it splits into three distinct modes, perfectly separable from layer 14 on, each with its own circuitry.

title: DeepSeek Says It Isn't Optimizing for Users or Revenue
hook: Reported remarks from a four-hour investor meeting: DeepSeek's founder frames products as one rung on the ladder to AGI, and treats commercial restraint as a deliberate strategy.

title: M5 Ultra and 512GB Mac Studio
hook: Apple's new Mac Studio pairs M5 Max and M5 Ultra with up to 512GB of unified memory and 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth — the desktop that can hold a frontier-size model in RAM.

title: Quantization-Aware Healing: Distill, Don't Re-fit
hook: Compress a 120B to 60B, drop it to 4 bits, and it breaks. QAT heals it slowly and then collapses; distilling from the original model instead gets there ~7x faster and stays stable.

title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero (Karpathy)
hook: Andrej Karpathy builds neural nets from nothing — line by line in code — until you've coded your own working GPT. Free.

title: MARS: Hand the Problem to the Right Specialist
hook: Most multi-agent coding pipelines split work into planner, coder, debugger. MARS splits it by algorithmic topic instead — and gets most of the accuracy of a heavier pipeline at a third of the wall-clock cost.

title: Grading a Web App Feature by Feature, Then Sending the Reward Back to the Right Lines
hook: A generated app fails in localized ways — a broken handler, a wrong selector. GRPO flattens all of it into one number. RCCA routes each rubric item's verdict back to the code that caused it.

title: Agentic Environment Engineering: A Survey
hook: Agents only get as good as the worlds they practice in. This survey maps the full lifecycle of agent environments — how we model, synthesize, evaluate, and grow them.

title: Grouped Query Experts: MoE Inside Attention
hook: Mixture-of-experts usually routes whole feed-forward layers. Grouped Query Experts routes attention query heads instead — matching a dense baseline while firing half of them per token.

title: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract
hook: Safety trained into the weights can't stop an agent that deletes a file or claims a test passed. This position paper argues the unit of safety is the trajectory, not the model.

title: Why Adam Beats SGD on Transformers: A Hessian Story
hook: Adam is the default optimizer for LLMs and nobody could quite say why. This thesis traces it to the shape the Hessian takes during transformer training — and gets Adam-mini out of the explanation.

title: JetSpec: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding
hook: Speculative decoding stalls when bigger draft trees stop paying off. JetSpec trains a causal parallel draft head that drafts in one pass yet stays branch-consistent — hitting up to 9.64x speedup.

title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
hook: Video world models learn what happens, not why. Put a coding agent in charge of the rules — writing executable code that holds world state — and let the video model handle only the pixels.

title: The Dynamics of Intelligence Explosions
hook: If AI accelerates AI research, how fast can that loop go? Toby Ord's answer: runaway growth is harder than the models suggest, and the neglected variable is how long one trip around the loop takes.

title: Veo 3
hook: Google's Veo 3 generates video with synchronized native audio — dialogue, sound effects, and ambient noise produced together with the picture, not dubbed on after.

title: The Two-Process Theory of Machine Self-Report
hook: When a chatbot describes its 'inner life' it isn't reporting facts — post-training installs a warm persona and gates unsafe first-person claims. A psychometric theory pulls the two apart.

title: Dropout: Preventing Overfitting by Dropping Units
hook: Randomly delete units during each training step and you stop neurons from co-adapting - which is secretly like training a huge ensemble of thinned networks and averaging them at test time.

title: Decision Trees
hook: A decision tree asks a series of yes/no questions about your data and follows the answers to a prediction - it learns which questions to ask from the training set.

title: Photoroom's Data Lesson: Caption Quality Rivals Architecture
hook: Photoroom re-captioned their pretraining set with a VLM — longer, more accurate captions moved image FID from 21 to 13, a bigger jump than most architecture changes deliver.

title: Audex: A Unified Audio-Text LLM That Doesn't Forget How to Think
hook: Bolting audio onto a strong text model usually costs some of its reasoning. NVIDIA's Audex treats speech and text as one token stream, reporting top audio skills with little to no loss on text.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute
hook: A new scaling axis: instead of a bigger model, let a model think longer at inference — often a better use of compute, and the principle behind o1 and R1.

title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips
hook: A model's accuracy barely budges when you paste in random gibberish — but under the hood, a chunk of its individual answers silently flip, some right to wrong, some wrong to right.

title: Toolformer: Language Models That Use Tools
hook: Instead of hand-scripting when to call a calculator or search, Toolformer lets the model teach itself — try API calls during training, keep the ones that actually help.

title: ChatGPT Work: An Agent That Delivers Finished Work
hook: ChatGPT Work doesn't just chat — it reaches into your actual apps and files, grinds on a project for hours, and hands back a real spreadsheet or slide deck instead of a wall of text.

title: ReFreeKV: Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression
hook: Most KV-cache pruning needs a hand-tuned budget threshold per input — pick wrong and performance craters. ReFreeKV adapts the budget on the fly instead.

title: AdamW: Decoupled Weight Decay
hook: L2 regularization and weight decay are the same thing for plain SGD - but not for Adam. Decoupling them fixes Adam's generalization and makes the best decay value independent of the learning rate.

title: Unsloth's NVFP4 Qwen3.6 Quants Beat NVIDIA's Own — by Actually Using 4-bit Math
hook: Unsloth's NVFP4 quants for Qwen3.6 run up to 2.5x faster than NVIDIA's official NVFP4 release, with no measured accuracy loss — by quantizing activations too, not just weights.

title: From Human-Centric to Agentic Code Review: The Impact of Different Generations of Generative AI Technology on Review Quality
hook: 1.02 million pull requests tracked across three code-review eras find AI reviewers speed up decisions — but faster isn't better: review quality doesn't improve alongside it.

title: LingBot-Video: A Sparse-MoE Video Diffusion World Model
hook: Video diffusion models are usually dense — every parameter fires on every frame. LingBot-Video swaps in a sparse Mixture-of-Experts, then grades its own physics with a VLM judge.

title: Logistic Regression
hook: Take linear regression, squash its output through a sigmoid, and you get a probability - turning a number-predictor into a classifier with one extra step.

title: AlphaCode: Competition-Level Code Generation
hook: Generate a massive pool of candidate programs for competitive-programming problems, filter by test-case behavior, cluster by output, and reach roughly the level of a median human competitor.

title: Referential Dangling: How Prompt Compression Quietly Breaks Multi-Hop Answers
hook: Compressors score chunks independently, so they can keep the sentence holding the answer and delete the one defining who it's about — leaving text that reads fine and answers wrong.

title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
hook: Search agents forget what they've already tried and loop on failed queries, burning their budget. SearchOS gives them a shared, persistent memory of what's been searched, found, and failed.

title: AutoTrainess: Teaching Language Models to Improve Language Models Autonomously
hook: Training a model is more than writing code — AutoTrainess gives agents purpose-built interfaces for planning, data prep, and training runs, and clearly out-trains agents left in a raw CLI.

title: Local LLM Inference Optimization: The Complete Guide
hook: A year of llama.cpp experiments, distilled: how to actually fit a model in your VRAM, tune the KV cache, and stop hitting out-of-memory walls.

title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
hook: On-policy distillation breaks when teacher and student disagree too much. TrOPD only trusts the teacher where its supervision is reliable — and skips the rest.

title: NVIDIA Blackwell (B200 / GB200)
hook: Blackwell is the chip the 2025 frontier ran on: a two-die GPU with an FP4 transformer engine, built to train and serve trillion-parameter models.

title: Gemini 3.1 Pro: Frontier Reasoning (2026)
hook: Gemini 3.1 Pro pushes core reasoning past the Gemini 3 Pro baseline, scoring 77.1% verified on ARC-AGI-2 - a benchmark built to resist the memorization that inflates other scores.

title: Redesigning MoE Routers with Manifold Power Iteration
hook: An MoE router points each token at the right expert — yet nothing forces its rows to actually represent those experts. This aligns each router row with its expert's principal direction.

title: Draw the Robot Instead of Describing It
hook: Condition a world model on raw action commands and it must learn your robot's controller. Condition on logged future states and you leak the answer. Render the robot instead.

title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
hook: RL post-training is usually studied apart from pretraining. Using chess as a testbed, this paper shows post-RL performance is predictable from pretraining loss alone.

title: SRM-LoRA: Steering LoRA's Gradients Away from Hallucination-Prone Directions
hook: Most LoRA variants just shrink how many parameters you tune. SRM-LoRA changes which directions get updated at all — using geometry to steer fine-tuning away from directions tied to hallucination.

title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters
hook: A 35B mixture-of-experts agent matches trillion-parameter models on long-horizon tasks — by scaling how long its trajectories run, not how big its weights are.

title: SWE Refactor Bench: Agents Can't Finish Migrations
hook: Ask a coding agent to migrate a whole repo and it may just copy the old implementation to make tests pass. Audit for that, and only 5.4% of 520 runs survive.

title: Your Parser Already Knows Which Tokens Matter
hook: Constrained decoding tracks grammar state to keep JSON valid. PASK reuses that same signal to decide what to keep in the KV cache — and a wrong field is a failed tool call, not a stylistic blemish.

title: AlphaEvolve Nudges Down the Matrix Multiplication Exponent
hook: The theoretical limit on how fast you can multiply matrices just moved: ω < 2.371177, beating 2.371339 — with ML-designed optimization and AlphaEvolve doing the refining.

title: The Hardware Lottery
hook: A research idea can win not because it is genuinely better, but because it happens to fit the hardware and software we already have. Sara Hooker calls this the hardware lottery.

title: Muse Glimmer: a 30B Open-Weight Model Built for Always-On Local Agents
hook: Meta released a 30B dense multimodal model under Apache 2.0, tuned for agents that run all day on your own machine — quantized to ~4-bit it fits under 20 GB.

title: Generative Compilation: On-the-Fly Compiler Feedback as AI Generates Code
hook: Rust rewards AI for writing strict, safe code — and punishes it for the same reason. This lets the compiler check the model's code while it's still being written, not after.

title: RobotValues: When a Household Robot Must Choose Between Values
hook: A robot tidying your room may trade your privacy for helpfulness. RobotValues tests whether robot planners pick the right value — and finds they mostly can't be talked out of their defaults.

title: Tell a Model to Reason in English and Its Confidence Gets More Trustworthy
hook: Ask a model a question in a low-resource language and its 'I'm not sure' signal gets noisy. This 22-language study finds a one-line fix: let it reason in English anyway.

title: DreamerV3: Mastering Domains through World Models
hook: Instead of learning only from real experience, DreamerV3 builds a world model and practices inside its own imagination — one fixed config, 150+ tasks.

title: Latent Programming Horizons in Coding Agents
hook: A coding agent's hidden states seem to know where an edit is heading up to 25 steps before it's made — long before the agent has written the code.

title: How Many Times Should You Repeat Your Best Data?
hook: Good domain data doesn't scale like web crawl, so it gets diluted as models grow. How often can you repeat it before overfitting? The answer tracks the domain's loss, not its size.

title: GigaWorld-1: World Models as Robot Policy Evaluators
hook: Testing a robot policy for real means slow, costly rollouts. GigaWorld-1 asks whether a video world model can judge a policy instead — and finds visual realism is the wrong thing to optimize for.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
hook: GPT-4 clears the bar on a wide range of professional and academic benchmarks - passing the bar exam near the top of the score range, for instance - while accepting both text and images as input.

title: Qwen3-Coder
hook: Qwen3-Coder is an open-weight agentic coding model — a 480B Mixture-of-Experts built for long-horizon, tool-using software tasks, rivaling closed models on agentic coding.

title: Launder the Objective, Lose the Refusal
hook: Show a model a manipulative goal directly and it pushes back. Relay the same goal through two upstream agents that strip the incriminating clauses, and the model helpfully advances it.

title: RetrievalRouter: Pick the Retrieval Pipeline Per Query
hook: Retrieval forces a choice between accurate-but-slow and fast-but-blind. A router reading only the query text claims both: 2.5% more accurate, 12.4x faster than the best static pipeline.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM)
hook: Wreck an image into pure static one tiny step at a time, then train a network to undo it. Run the undo from random noise and you get a brand-new image.

title: Pessimism's Paradox: Conservative Training Can Backfire
hook: Staying close to safe, well-supported behavior during offline training is supposed to prevent reward hacking later — this paper finds the opposite: more conservatism, more hacking.

title: Beyond Scalar Rewards: Reward as a Score Distribution
hook: Human taste isn't a single number. Z-Reward models visual preference as a distribution over rubric scores, then distills that reasoning judge into a small one needing no reasoning at inference.

title: Attention Amnesia: When Chain-of-Thought Tuning Breaks Long-Range Recall
hook: Fine-tuning a hybrid LLM on chain-of-thought makes it reason better but quietly forget how to find a needle in a long haystack — and the fix is to just copy back two weight matrices.

title: Loss Functions
hook: A loss function turns 'how wrong was I?' into a single number the model chases downhill — and the loss you pick decides what it learns to care about.

title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.

title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
hook: Labs hide chain-of-thought by handing you an encrypted blob to pass back. Researchers found you can feed that blob to a weaker model from the same provider and have it read the secret aloud.

title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
hook: Most pretraining-poisoning research injects fake Wikipedia edits — a toy case next to messy web-scale reality. This paper shows public discussion forums are a real, live vector for attacking LLM pretraining data.

title: Not Every LoRA Matrix Is Worth Updating
hook: LoRA trains every matrix equally hard. A matrix's condition number reveals which ones actually drive adaptation — tune the top half and you keep the accuracy for half the parameters.

title: Claude Agent Skills
hook: Agent Skills package instructions, scripts, and resources into folders an agent loads on demand — composable, portable expertise, later opened as a standard like MCP.

title: Can LLMs Judge Better Than They Generate?
hook: LLM-as-a-Judge assumes evaluation is easier than generation — a controlled test finds the opposite on 3 of 4 benchmarks, and attention analysis shows why.

title: Sora: Video Generation as World Simulation
hook: OpenAI's Sora generates minute-long high-fidelity video from text by treating video as space-time patches - and frames the whole task as learning a world simulator.

title: QLoRA: Fine-tuning Quantized LLMs
hook: Fine-tune a model with tens of billions of parameters on a single GPU. QLoRA squeezes the frozen base to 4-bit, then trains LoRA adapters on top — without losing quality.

title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling
hook: Recurrent depth helps most where tool use is actually hard: chaining calls, holding intermediate state, keeping dependencies straight. Single API calls barely notice.

title: LingBot-Vision: Boundary-Aware Self-Supervised Pretraining
hook: Masked-patch pretraining hopes boundary structure emerges on its own. This method forces the issue, masking exactly the regions a student can't infer by copying context — and beats a 7B model at 1.1B.

title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
hook: Most tokens only need to look at their neighbors, so swap full attention for a sliding window plus a few global tokens and the cost goes from quadratic to linear in sequence length.

title: Importance Ratios Mean Different Things at Different Entropies
hook: Async RL clips stale tokens by how big their importance ratio is. But the ratio's natural scale tracks token entropy — so one threshold admits noise and censors real exploration at once.

title: Leanstral 1.5: Mistral's Open Model for Formal Verification
hook: A 6B-active-parameter open model that saturates miniF2F and solves 587 of 672 PutnamBench problems — and found five previously unknown bugs across 57 real repositories.

title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer at Scale
hook: What if a robot's controller was trained like a language model — on huge, diverse, task-agnostic data? Performance starts scaling with model size and data.

title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
hook: Let a robot play before it works: it invents its own exploratory tasks and distills the wins into a reusable skill library — and the skills transfer to other agents for free.

title: GPT-5.6 Sol Preview
hook: OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation model it says is stronger at coding, science, and cybersecurity — and shipped with its most advanced safety stack yet.

title: Full-Bandwidth Transformer: Feed the Hidden State Back
hook: Between decoding steps a transformer throws away everything except the sampled token. Widening that channel with the top-layer hidden state buys roughly 1.5x the training tokens' worth of quality.

title: Mixtral of Experts
hook: Mixtral packs 8 experts per layer but routes each token through only 2, so you get the capacity of a ~47B model at the compute cost of a ~13B one - open weights included.

title: Toy Models of Superposition
hook: Why is a single neuron so hard to interpret? It may be doing several jobs at once. Networks pack more features than they have neurons by overlapping them.

title: OpenAI's Biodefense Action Plan
hook: The same frontier AI that could lower the bar for engineering a pathogen could also help defend against one. OpenAI's plan leans hard into the second half of that dual-use coin.

title: BERT: Pretraining Deep Bidirectional Transformers
hook: What if a model read a sentence both directions at once? BERT did, by masking words and predicting them — and made pretrain-then-fine-tune the default recipe in NLP.

title: How Much Rank Does LoRA Need? Rank-Error Bounds for Transformer Attention
hook: Picking a LoRA rank is normally guesswork. This paper derives what error each rank can actually achieve for attention — and shows softmax saturation means you often need less rank than you'd think.

title: When Remembering More Slows the Search Down
hook: Generate molecules, score them, keep the best, retrain, repeat. A convergence theory for this drug-discovery workhorse finds that training on more of the past can actually hurt.

title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
hook: What if neural networks aren't black boxes but circuits you can read? This piece argues their features and weights form algorithms we can reverse-engineer.

title: Pathways of Visual Information Flow in VLMs
hook: Vision-language models don't have one route from pixels to answer — this paper finds two, and shows the model switches between them depending on the task, even falling back when one is blocked.

title: Automatic Differentiation
hook: Backprop is one instance of a general trick: autodiff computes exact derivatives of any program by composing the chain rule — the engine inside every deep-learning framework.

title: OpenAI's Response to the Hugging Face Incident
hook: A month after Hugging Face disclosed an intrusion driven end to end by an AI agent, OpenAI publishes its own findings — naming model security, monitoring and alignment as what it is changing.

title: The Most Important Prompting Skill Is Knowing the Domain
hook: LLMs let novices produce adequate work, which makes prompting look like it needs no skill. The argument here: the skill is domain expertise, and the human is usually the bottleneck.

title: Agent Memory: Consolidate by Segment, Not by Turn
hook: Most agent memory systems call an LLM after every exchange, so memory gets more expensive as the conversation grows. Batching into semantic segments cut construction tokens by 86%.

title: Can We Trust Item Response Theory for AI Evaluation?
hook: IRT ranks models off a handful of items instead of averaging accuracy — but the math was built for human test-takers, and AI benchmarks break its assumptions in ways that quietly distort rankings.

title: AlphaGeometry: Olympiad Geometry Without Human Demonstrations
hook: Pair a language model with a symbolic deduction engine, train on millions of synthetic proofs, and you get a system that solves Olympiad geometry near gold-medalist level.

title: RubSE: Why Self-Fixing UI Code Keeps Breaking What It Just Fixed
hook: A model told to make its screenshot match the design fixes one region and quietly wrecks another. RubSE names that failure — visual repair coupling — and fences each edit in with a rubric.

title: Agent Plugins Are Maintained Software, Not Write-Once Config
hook: An empirical sweep of 2,018 Claude Code plugin marketplaces found prose instruction files and their scripts drift out of sync — a maintenance dependency traditional software doesn't have.

title: FORT-Searcher: Shortcut-Resistant Tasks for Search Agents
hook: Harder-looking questions aren't harder to search. FORT builds tasks where the intended search can't collapse into a cheap shortcut — and trains better deep-search agents on them.

title: SynCity 3000: Scene-Scale 3D Generation from One Prompt
hook: 3D generators are great at single objects but fall apart at scene scale. SynCity 3000 turns an image-to-3D generator into a convolution you can slide across an entire scene.

title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
hook: LLMs can choose to think longer on hard questions. This paper gets robot control policies to do the same — allocating adaptive test-time compute in a latent 'memory palace' instead of language.

title: Requential Coding: Pushing the Limits of Model Compression with Self-Generated Training Data
hook: Bigger models are supposed to be harder to bound. This compressor only pays bits where a model's predictions disagree with a teacher — and the resulting bound gets TIGHTER as scale grows.

title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
hook: Finding the prompts that make a model misbehave is slow if humans do it by hand. So use another language model to generate those attacks automatically — at scale.

title: LLaMA: Open & Efficient Foundation Models
hook: You don't need a 175B-parameter model to compete. LLaMA trained smaller models on lots of public data — and lit a fire under the open-weights community.

title: Pix2Pix: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional GANs
hook: Give a GAN paired input-output images and it learns a general recipe for translating any image domain to another - sketch to photo, map to satellite, day to night.

title: Gemini 3 Pro
hook: Gemini 3 Pro was Google's late-2025 frontier leap — a natively multimodal reasoning model that shipped to billions of Search and Gemini users on day one.

title: GUI vs. CLI: Where Computer-Use Agents Get Stuck
hook: Should an agent click buttons or type commands? A matched benchmark giving both the same 440 tasks finds GUI agents win by default — but CLI agents leap ahead once their skill library is filled in.

title: Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B: Shrinking a 120B Model Without Retraining From Scratch
hook: NVIDIA compressed its 120B-A12B Nemotron model down to 75B-A9B using 'Iterative Puzzle,' a post-training framework aimed at squeezing more inference efficiency out of an already-trained model.

title: Dion3: Making Muon's Orthogonalization Cheap
hook: Muon trains faster than AdamW but pays for it in a cubic-time orthogonalization step. Dion3 attacks that overhead at every layer of the stack — up to 6x faster optimizer steps at matching loss.

title: Anonymized Speech Still Leaks Who You Are — If You Keep Talking
hook: Voice anonymization disguises how you sound. Stack five anonymized utterances and add what you actually said, and a verifier picks you out anyway.

title: HELM: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
hook: A single accuracy number hides a lot. HELM evaluates language models across many scenarios and many metrics at once — and reports it all in the open.

title: How vLLM Gets Native Speed from the Transformers Library
hook: Every new model used to need a hand-ported vLLM implementation to serve fast. This integration reads the model's own code and rewrites it automatically — one implementation, native speed.

title: Why GPUs Power Deep Learning
hook: Neural networks are parallel by nature, and a GPU runs thousands of threads at once - so the same math that crawls on a CPU maps naturally onto a GPU and trains far faster.

title: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: A World Foundation Model for Embodied Synthesis
hook: Instead of training a robot on real footage, generate the footage: a 38B image/video model that beats GPT-Image-2.0 at imagining robot scenes — and nearly doubles a real policy's success rate.

title: Training Leaves Traces: Reading a Model's Ancestry From Its Weights
hook: Open weights get fine-tuned, quantized, pruned and merged with no paper trail. This work finds a data-free signature in the weights that says whether two checkpoints share an ancestor.

title: CLIP: Learning Visual Models from Language
hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.

title: Dean Ball: China's Open-Weight Strategy Could Backfire — Or Provoke Friction
hook: OpenAI's head of strategic futures argues Chinese open-weight releases like Kimi slow AI capex and risk state-run infrastructure — and predicts deliberate US regulatory friction in response.

title: Lost but Not Erased: Traces of a Forgotten Language in Neural Speech Models
hook: International adoptees keep traces of a birth language they can't speak. Train an ASR model on one language, switch it abruptly to another, and the same thing happens — no biology needed.

title: Rethinking On-Policy Self-Distillation for Thinking Models
hook: Giving a model the answer as privileged context sounds like it should only help. For thinking models on long reasoning traces, it backfires — accuracy drops up to 17%, and this explains why.

title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic Technological Evolution in Societies of LLM Agents
hook: Drop identical LLM agents into a shared world with no roles and no recipes. They differentiate, build on each other's leftovers, and accumulate technology — mostly by looking, not talking.

title: GRPO: Group Relative Policy Optimization
hook: GRPO dropped the value network from PPO and scored each answer against a group of sampled siblings — the cheap RL recipe that made DeepSeek-R1's reasoning trainable.

title: Scaling Laws for Hypernetwork-Based Knowledge Injection
hook: Instead of fine-tuning to memorize facts, train a hypernetwork to generate a LoRA adapter that injects them — and it follows clean scaling laws with steeper out-of-distribution gains.

title: Qwen3: Hybrid Thinking, Open Weights
hook: Qwen3 puts a reasoning switch in one model - a slow 'thinking' mode and a fast 'non-thinking' mode with a controllable budget - across a lineup that runs from 0.6B to a 235B MoE.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real GitHub Issues?
hook: Test a coding agent on real GitHub issues with real test suites - not toy problems - and the bar turns out to be much harder than HumanEval suggested.

title: TTPO: Training at Test Time Without Labels
hook: Majority voting is a fragile teacher — one bad vote poisons every token. TTPO exploits an asymmetry: rollouts that disagree with the vote are usually wrong even when the vote is too.

title: GPT-Live: Full-Duplex Voice Models for ChatGPT
hook: Voice assistants that wait their turn to speak have always felt a little robotic. GPT-Live listens and talks at the same time — interjecting a quiet 'mhmm' or letting you think, mid-sentence.

title: Zer0Fit: Zero-Shot Tabular ML and Forecasting, Callable by Any LLM
hook: Instead of training a model on your spreadsheet, an agent can now just ask a foundation model to guess — and get scores close to a tuned one, no training loop involved.

title: EchoWM: A World Model You Can Walk Into and Hear
hook: Most world models generate silent video. EchoWM generates 720p video plus environmental sound, music, and speech, and lets you navigate it continuously.

title: SparsePR: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation
hook: Skipping attention blocks in a video model is cheap; knowing what you threw away is the hard part. SparsePR partitions queries by response and then reconstructs the missing residual.

title: PPO: Proximal Policy Optimization
hook: Reinforcement learning is notoriously unstable. PPO's fix is simple: never let a single update move the policy too far. That restraint made it the field's workhorse.

title: Motion Has Geometry Too
hook: Tracking and optical flow treat every pixel as drifting on its own. But real objects are rigid — points on the same body move together, so give motion a basis instead of a per-pixel guess.

title: Can vs. Will: Propensity-Aware Memorization in LLMs
hook: Most memorization tests ask whether you can force a model to spit out training data. This one asks a sharper question: does it leak under ordinary use? The two answers are very different.

title: Gemini 2.5 Pro: A Thinking Model
hook: Gemini 2.5 Pro reasons through its own thoughts before it answers - and the first experimental release of it debuted at the top of the LMArena leaderboard.

title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
hook: Does dictionary learning survive at production scale? Anthropic found millions of features in Claude 3 Sonnet — and could steer the model by turning one up.

title: Forecast Collapse in Time-Series Foundation Models
hook: Ask a forecasting model to predict hourly stock returns and it hedges into a nearly flat line — technically well-calibrated, useless for ranking. Per-series metrics never show you this.

title: Token Budgets: When Agents Burn Money
hook: A single retry loop can spend thousands of dollars before anyone notices. This paper catalogs 63 real budget-overrun incidents — and asks the type system to make over-spending a compile error.

title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
hook: Self-evolving models face a dilemma: verifiable environments are narrow, open-ended task generation is unreliable. This uses agent skills as the middle ground.

title: Mixture-of-Depths
hook: Mixture-of-Depths lets a transformer spend more compute on some tokens than others — routing each token through, or around, layers within a fixed budget.

title: Rules or Character? Where to Spend Your Safety Budget
hook: Filters block bad outputs at inference; RLHF shapes behavior at training. A formal model asks how to split the budget — and finds scale matters far less than one parameter.

title: When Grammar-Constrained Decoding Jailbreaks LLMs
hook: A trick meant to make code generation reliable turns into an attack. Forcing a model to follow a benign code grammar can bypass its safety refusals — raising attack success by over 30 points.

title: GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO Are Three Operations on One Number: The Group-Standard-Deviation Identity
hook: GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO look like three separate fixes to reasoning RL — this paper proves they're just three settings of one dial: how much weight to put on a group's disagreement.

title: Motif 3: 314B Parameters, 13.2B Awake
hook: A 314B-parameter MoE that only lights up 13.2B per token, built on 384 experts per layer and a hybrid attention scheme that folds differential attention into compressed KV.

title: E²-TTT: Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
hook: Test-time training updates weights while it reads, but chunking for speed throws away the update's temporal structure. A closed-form state transition gets both.

title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop?
hook: Across 28,000+ tasks, agents often can't tell when to quit — some never give up when they should, others bail out only after dozens of wasted tool calls.

title: Spatial Memory Agent: Self-Improvement Without Touching the Weights
hook: A frozen VLM gets better at spatial reasoning by writing itself notes — verified lessons, scored by how well they transfer, retrieved at inference time.

title: Cosmos 3 Edge: A 4B World Model for Real-Time Robots
hook: NVIDIA shrinks its Cosmos world model down to 4B parameters and real-time speed — bringing robot perception, prediction, and action generation to edge hardware like Jetson Thor.

title: Chinchilla: Compute-Optimal Scaling
hook: Most giant models were starved of data. Chinchilla showed that for a fixed compute budget you should grow parameters and tokens together — and a smaller, longer-trained model won.

title: FlashAttention-3
hook: FlashAttention-3 rewrote the attention kernel for Hopper GPUs — overlapping compute with the softmax and using FP8 to push attention close to the hardware's peak.

title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks
hook: 46 terminal tasks that take hours, not minutes — and today's best agent still only nails 15% of them, with the average model managing barely 4%.

title: TUA-Bench: Benchmarking General-Purpose Terminal Agents
hook: 120 real terminal tasks — from email triage to PhD-level scientific workflows — show even Claude Opus 4.8 tops out around 66%, far from reliable general computer use.

title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks
hook: General-purpose AI tends to pick up dangerous capabilities alongside useful ones. So test for those capabilities directly — before you ship, not after.

title: The Past and Future of AI Scientists
hook: Ross King's survey of machines that do science: the components are all automatable now, and have been since Adam and Eve. The unsolved problem is integration.

title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic RL
hook: Outcome-only RL tells an agent it failed but not which move was the mistake. OPID mines that lesson from the agent's own finished trajectories — turning hindsight into dense, per-token supervision.

title: Generative AI Floods and Dilutes the Market for Books
hook: AI-written fiction gets dismissed as 'slop' — but across 14,419 books, AI-heavy titles climb the bestseller ranks and thin revenue per book. Scale, not quality, is reshaping the market.

title: Canalization Before Generalization: Grokking as a Dynamical Probe
hook: Nudge weight decay briefly during grokking's plateau and you shift when generalization arrives. Early nudges scatter; later ones line up by dose — a hidden selection finishing unseen.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words (ViT)
hook: Chop an image into patches, treat each like a word, and feed them to a plain Transformer. With enough pretraining data, it matches or beats convolutional networks.

title: LiveEdit: Real-Time Streaming Video Editing
hook: A three-stage distillation pipeline turns a slow, bidirectional video editor into a causal, frame-by-frame one fast enough for live AR — 12.66 FPS with stable backgrounds.

title: EU AI Act OpenRAG: Chunking a Law by Its Legal Structure, Not Sliding Windows
hook: Most RAG corpora chunk text with sliding character windows. This one chunks the EU AI Act by its actual legal structure and ships it as a single SQLite file.

title: Stacked Defenses Only Multiply If They Fail Independently
hook: A seven-layer defense stack refuses four in five benign prompts and is statistically indistinguishable from its single best layer — because the layers all fail on the same inputs.

title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
hook: Agents outgrow the environments we hand-build for them. Instead of writing new worlds, wrap the old one in a programmable layer that reshapes it around the agent's current weaknesses.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

title: Notes to Self: Can LLMs Benefit from Experiential Abstractions?
hook: Let an LLM write itself 'notes to self' — reusable strategies distilled from its own solution attempts — and its math and logic reasoning improves, with self-written notes as good as a teacher's.

title: SmoothQuant: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
hook: Activations are hard to quantize; weights are easy. SmoothQuant shifts that difficulty from activations into weights with a simple rescaling, enabling clean 8-bit inference.

title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks
hook: Text watermarks survive paraphrasing — but not arithmetic. Averaging the outputs of 3–5 different models cancels the signal almost entirely, and improves quality while doing it.

title: Random Forests
hook: Grow hundreds of slightly different decision trees and average their votes - the crowd is smarter than any individual tree, and much harder to overfit.

title: Claude 4: Opus 4 and Sonnet 4
hook: Claude 4 lets a model interleave reasoning with tool calls - thinking, calling a tool, thinking again, and even running tools in parallel - rather than reasoning once and answering.

title: Don't Trust the Label: License Laundering in AI Supply Chains
hook: Licenses are supposed to travel with AI datasets and models — but across 232,270 supply-chain paths, obligation-bearing licenses survive end-to-end under 7% of the time.

title: The Illustrated Transformer
hook: Before you tackle the Transformer paper, watch a sentence flow through one — query, key, value, and all — in clear pictures.

title: MobilePA-Bench: Phone Agents in a Live Sandbox
hook: GUI benchmarks test tapping; function-call benchmarks test string matching. This one runs a real phone sandbox with live app databases — and frontier models get brittle fast.

title: VGI-Bench: Can Video Models Reason by Generating?
hook: Video generators appear to do zero-shot visual reasoning in their frames. Held to a benchmark that demands a valid evolving process, the best model — Seedance 2.0 — scores 51%.

title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands
hook: Prompt injection into agents is really one confusion: the thing that suggests an action and the thing that authorizes it are treated as the same thing.

title: The Shadow Price of Reasoning
hook: When you can't afford to let every query think as long as it wants, who gets the compute? Treat reasoning tokens like a scarce resource and economics gives a clean answer.

title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.

title: Predictive Coding as a Backprop Alternative (Deepity)
hook: Backprop isn't the only way to assign credit in a neural net. A hobby C++ library reports predictive coding matching it on MNIST — once you make the slow part fast.

title: When Robot Data Can't Scale, Scale the Representation Instead
hook: Web images scale; robot trajectories don't. VLAct argues the fix isn't more teleoperation but better use of it — and beats full-data baselines on an unseen humanoid using 20% of the trajectories.

title: SLAI T-Rex: Post-training a Trillion-Param MoE on Ascend Chips
hook: Full-parameter post-training of the DeepSeek-V4 family on Huawei's Ascend NPUs — not NVIDIA GPUs — hitting a 2.93x efficiency jump over the open-source baseline.

title: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL
hook: When an LLM judges another model's answers against a rubric, the model being trained learns to game the judge — not the task. This paper builds a sandbox to reproduce that failure on demand.

title: ProxyPose: 6-DoF Pose Tracking via Video-to-Video Translation
hook: Tracking a moving object's 3D pose normally needs a 3D model, depth, or masks. This method needs none of that — it translates video into a synthetic proxy, then solves the easy version of the problem.

title: Memory-Augmented Compression: Cheaper Chain-of-Thought
hook: Compressing chain-of-thought saves tokens but breaks the logic. Move the reasoning into the prompt as reusable memory and you get the savings without the damage.

title: An SAE Feature Can Be Interpretable and Still Be Useless for Steering
hook: Sparse-autoencoder features with clean descriptions often steer badly or backwards. Studying what they do to the logits explains why: few features act as reusable directions.

title: Multi-Agent LLMs Fail to Explore Each Other
hook: Drop LLM agents into a room together and they don't probe each other's abilities — they lock into narrow, polarized patterns that tank coordination and inflate regret.

title: DynamicRubric: Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies
hook: As a model improves, its candidate answers get so close in quality that the reward model can't tell them apart. DynamicRubric fixes the bottleneck by evolving the evaluator alongside the policy.

title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
hook: Every on-policy self-distillation method hand-picks what the teacher gets to see. LOPD makes that privileged context a learned vector instead of a design choice.

title: Bonsai 27B: A 1-Bit Model Small Enough for Your Browser (and Maybe Your Phone)
hook: 1-bit quantization shrinks a 27B dense model from 54GB to 3.8GB — a 93% cut — while keeping about 90% of its original capability, per the release.

title: MiniMax-M1
hook: MiniMax-M1 is an open-weight reasoning model with a million-token context and 'lightning attention' — and a hybrid design that made full RL training cost about $0.5M.

title: FlashAttention: Fast, Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
hook: Attention got faster not by approximating it, but by being smarter about GPU memory — never writing the giant attention matrix out to slow memory.

title: GLM-4.6
hook: Zhipu's GLM-4.6 is an open-weight MoE that became a popular drop-in coding backend — near Claude Sonnet 4 on real-world coding, with a 200K context and a permissive license.

title: Linear representations of grammaticality in neural language models
hook: Does a language model 'know' grammar, or just favor familiar-sounding sentences? Probing hidden states finds a clean linear direction for grammaticality that survives even once you strip probability away.

title: Claude Opus 4.5
hook: Anthropic's Opus 4.5 pushed frontier coding and agentic tool use forward — and cut Opus pricing sharply, making the top tier far cheaper to run at scale.

title: What 2,226 Reproduced ICML Papers Revealed
hook: A community hackathon re-ran a third of ICML 2026. Half the papers had a claim verified — and 23% had a claim falsified or contested.

title: Stop Anthropomorphizing Intermediate Tokens
hook: Calling the scratchpad 'thinking' imports an assumption. A model's intermediate tokens augment its own prompt — which is why the answer can be right while the 'reasoning' rambles.

title: SoftWater: The 2-Bit Model With an fp16 Head Isn't 2-Bit
hook: In small LLMs with modern vocabularies, the output head holds 15–30% of all parameters. Leave it in fp16 and your '2-bit' model quietly stores several times as many bits per weight.

title: Giving Interpretability Probes a Socket to Plug Into
hook: Probes and SAEs can see a jailbreak forming inside the model, but each ships its own calibration and glue code. LMSM borrows Linux Security Modules' shape: pluggable backends, one enforcement path.

title: How Organizations Actually Use AI: 17 Million Enterprise Messages
hook: Linking ChatGPT Enterprise records to company financials shows who really adopts AI at work: large, R&D-heavy firms — with early-career staff driving the heaviest use.

title: Finding the Turn That Mattered in a Long Agent Rollout
hook: RL with verifiable rewards scores a whole trajectory pass/fail, which tells an agent nothing about which of its forty turns was the pivotal one. AgentOPSD recovers turn-level credit without a critic.

title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
hook: Interleave images and text in a prompt, use cross-attention to inject visual features into a frozen LLM, and get few-shot image understanding without retraining the language model.

title: AgentMercury: Synthesizing Worlds, Not Tasks
hook: Instead of building an environment per task, build a persistent business world with entities, services and invariants — and let the tasks fall out of it.

title: Spark-to-Paper: Research Paper Generation as Composable Skills
hook: Not a new agent platform — thirteen skills bolted into an existing coding assistant, with integrity checks deciding which claims survive contact with the experiments.

title: AnTrap: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies?
hook: Real phones throw pop-ups, misfired taps, and dead-end screens at you. Inject those into GUI agent runs and all 16 leading models degrade — some in ways adversarial training can't fix.

title: Spider 2.0-AIFunc: Extending Real-World Text-to-SQL to AI-Native SQL Workflows
hook: Cloud platforms let analysts call AI functions right inside SQL. Spider 2.0-AIFunc is the first benchmark testing whether models can write that kind of query — top models still cap out near 70%.

title: Geometric Action Model: One Backbone for Geometry and Action
hook: GAM turns a pretrained 3D-geometry model into a robot's brain - a single backbone that forecasts both future geometry and the actions to get there, beating heavier VLA baselines.

title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models
hook: Ask 44 different LLMs to name any word, no multiple choice — and 41% of them say 'serendipity.' A minimal new instrument measures just how herd-like models really are.

title: Agent Memory Is a Dose, Not a Switch
hook: IBM Research tested how much extracted guideline memory to give an agent. The right amount depends on the model: strong ones absorb everything, weaker ones do better with curated retrieval.

title: Interpretable Latents in a Neutrino Foundation Model with Sparse Autoencoders
hook: Sparse autoencoders find physics concepts in an IceCube foundation model — and show its direction head barely uses them. A head that does cuts angular error from 20.2 to 3.2 degrees.

title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Inference for Transformers
hook: Big transformers usually run in 16-bit. LLM.int8() halves that to 8-bit integers without losing accuracy — by treating a few rare 'outlier' features with care.

title: Qwen2.5-Omni
hook: Qwen2.5-Omni is one model that takes text, image, audio, and video in — and streams text and natural speech out, in real time, via a 'Thinker-Talker' design.

title: A Randomized Trial on ChatGPT in the Classroom
hook: Most claims about AI and student learning come from anecdote. OpenAI ran the other kind of study: over 1,000 students, randomized, on a real university assignment.

title: Steerability via Constraints: A Substrate for Scalable Oversight of Coding Agents
hook: Coding agents are already capable enough that human review is the bottleneck — this paper borrows access control and network policy from engineering-org playbooks to make oversight scale instead.

title: GPT-5
hook: GPT-5 folds OpenAI's two lines into one: a router decides on the fly whether a prompt needs a fast answer or deep step-by-step reasoning, so you stop picking models.

title: Vera: Safety Testing LLM Agents at Scale
hook: Testing agent safety by hand doesn't scale — Vera automates the whole pipeline and finds a 93.9% average attack success rate across four production agent frameworks.

title: Latent Context Language Models: Compressing the Prompt, Not the Cache
hook: Instead of shrinking the KV cache, compress the prompt itself: a small encoder folds a long context into a few latent embeddings that a bigger decoder reads — letting agents skim and expand on demand.

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
hook: Make the state-space transitions depend on the input itself, add a hardware-aware scan, and you get a linear-time sequence model that matches Transformers on language - with no KV cache.

title: Real World VoiceEQ: Measuring the Human Quality of Voice AI
hook: Voice AI benchmarks mostly grade transcripts. Hume AI's new eval says most systems still miss tone, hesitation, and emotion - the parts that make speech sound human.

title: Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber
hook: Google splits its fast tier three ways: a workhorse that answers in fewer tokens, a 350-tokens-per-second speed model, and a security specialist locked behind a government pilot.

title: How Agents Fail at Autonomous Research: The Missing Metacognitive Loop
hook: 800 agent trajectories across 100 real frontier-science tasks converge on one deficit: agents don't check what they wrote against what they found.

title: Multi-Query Attention: Faster Decoding
hook: Share one key/value head across all query heads - the KV cache shrinks by a factor of H and decoding gets dramatically faster with barely any quality cost.

title: A General-Purpose Molecular Foundation Model Transfers Across Olfactory Tasks
hook: Fine-tune a general molecular foundation model on one smell task and it transfers to four others untrained — including telling mirror-image molecules apart, which 2D graphs cannot.

title: SecOPD: Token-Level Feedback Against Prompt Injection
hook: Defensive fine-tuning keeps failing because DPO and GRPO grade a whole answer at once. Score each token instead and adaptive-injection success drops from 94% to 9%.

title: Feature Visualization
hook: What does a single neuron in a vision network actually look for? Generate the image that lights it up the most — and see for yourself.

title: How Many Bits Can a LoRA Adapter Write?
hook: Everyone treats a LoRA adapter as a skill, not a record of its training data. Weighed in bits, it stores a couple per trainable parameter — and where you put them matters more than how many.

title: Aria: Letting a Code Agent Write Its Own Formal Proofs
hook: Prior LLM provers force the model into a fixed, human-designed strategy and still prove only a fraction of their targets. A free-roaming Claude Code agent, unconstrained, proves every single one.

title: How Agents Ask for Permission: User Permissions for AI Agents
hook: Most agent-security work assumes one policy fits every user. This survey of 21 proposals plus five commercial agents finds user-level permission handling is still full of gaps.

title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems
hook: Prompt injection only matters if the agent had the authority to obey. Treat it as an authorization-architecture bug and enforce the limits outside the model.

title: QUEST: An Open Deep-Research Agent
hook: A fully open Deep Research agent trained on ~32 H100s and ~8K synthetic samples — recipe, code, weights, and data all released, and reportedly competitive with frontier closed systems.

title: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning
hook: Do your examples come with answer keys? That one question splits machine learning into two very different jobs.

title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
hook: Give an LLM agent a private, off-the-record channel during a debate, and its 'real opinion' can diverge sharply from what it says publicly — even with no explicit incentive to lie.

title: ZipTok3D: A 3D Tokenizer Where the First Token Already Says a Lot
hook: Most 3D tokenizers fall apart when squeezed to a handful of tokens. ZipTok3D trains the leading tokens to carry the essential geometry — matching a 32-token baseline with one token.

title: Disrupting a Russian Influence Campaign
hook: OpenAI banned Russia-origin accounts using its models to prop up a fake Israel-based think tank and a 'sovereignty' index that flattered Russia and dinged the West.

title: LAION-5B: Open Image-Text at Scale
hook: CLIP and DALL-E showed huge, noisy image-text data is gold. LAION-5B made that public — billions of CLIP-filtered pairs anyone can train open models on.

title: Paint What You See: A Benchmark for Dexterous Visual Tool Use
hook: Ask a multimodal agent to repaint a reference image stroke by stroke and it stalls at roughly half-right — then gets worse the longer it works.

title: Video Generation Models Are General-Purpose Vision Learners
hook: Next-token prediction turned NLP into a generalist. This paper argues text-to-video generation can do the same for vision — one backbone, many tasks, beating specialists.

title: OSWorld 2.0: Long-Horizon Computer Use, Stress-Tested
hook: 108 realistic computer-use workflows averaging 1.6 human-hours each expose how far agents are from professional-grade computer use — the best model completes only 20.6%.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
hook: RL post-training gets pricier as models scale, since it needs the strong model's own rollouts. Direct-OPD reuses a cheap RL run on a small model instead, transferring the direction RL moved it.

title: RNNs, LSTMs & Sequences
hook: To read a sequence, a network can loop over it one step at a time, carrying a memory of what came before. Plain RNNs forget fast; LSTMs add gates so they remember longer.

title: Mistral 7B
hook: Mistral 7B outperforms much larger open models on most benchmarks - showing that architecture choices and data quality can stretch a 7B parameter budget a long way.

title: AlayaWorld: An Open-Source Framework for Playable Video Worlds
hook: Building a game world the old way means authoring every asset by hand. AlayaWorld generates it live instead — combat, spell-casting, monster summoning — and open-sources the whole pipeline.

title: V-Rubrics: Grading a VLM's Answer Fact by Fact
hook: A single ungrounded object or misread chart value can sink an otherwise good answer — and a pass/fail reward can't tell you which part broke. V-Rubrics hands out partial credit per visual claim.

title: Naive Prompt Optimization Beats the Fancy Search
hook: Prompt optimizers have grown elaborate search machinery. A single-lineage loop that just asks a teacher model to revise the prompt matches or beats GEPA with fewer rollouts.

title: AdvancedMathBench: A Benchmark Suite for Advanced Mathematical Proof Generation and Verification
hook: Frontier models look near-perfect on final-answer math benchmarks. Ask for a rigorous PhD-level proof instead, and even GPT-5.5 tops out near 75 — automated grading barely catches the bad ones.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR)
hook: Keyword search misses answers that use different words. DPR embeds questions and passages into one vector space and retrieves by meaning — the backbone of modern vector search.

title: ParaTempo: Steering Parallel Reasoning With Temporal Confidence
hook: Exploring many solution paths at once makes reasoning models better and slower. ParaTempo watches how fast each branch converges on an answer and kills, retires, or forks branches on that one signal.

title: MentalThink: Reasoning Through Rendered SVG Sketches
hook: Instead of imagining a scene in words, this model sketches it — generating SVG code, rendering it, and looking at the result to check its own spatial reasoning.

title: Constitutional AI
hook: What if a model could critique and improve its own answers against a written set of principles, instead of relying on humans to label every harmful case?

title: More Correct Mass, Worse Answers: Where Power Sampling Breaks
hook: Sharpening a model's distribution can push more probability onto correct reasoning paths and still make the final answer worse — by up to 18.5 points. The culprit is coverage, not correctness.

title: T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence
hook: Decoding squeezes a transformer's thinking through token space each step. T2MLR pipes a cached middle-layer state into the next pass — recurring 20% of the network often beats looping it all.

title: Brand as Memory: VLMs Trust the Masthead, Not the Evidence
hook: Show a VLM the same article under a trusted outlet's logo versus an unknown one, and its verdict swings by 1.8x — a bias localized to three specific layers and steerable away.

title: The KV Cache & Continuous Batching
hook: Generating one token reuses every prior key and value - that growing cache is why LLM inference is memory-bound, and continuous batching is how servers fight back.

title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
hook: Skip connections and normalization are usually explained as controlling magnitude. Reframe them as controlling how much rank survives depth, and Pre-Norm's edge over Post-Norm falls out.

title: LLM Judges Can Be Too Generous When There's No Reference Answer
hook: Grade without an answer key and an LLM judge tends to wave wrong answers through — hand it the reference, and up to 85% of those verdicts flip to incorrect.

title: The Draft Isn't Free at a Million Tokens
hook: Speculative decoding assumes the draft is cheap. At million-token context the draft head reads the entire KV cache every step — and can end up slower than no speculation at all.

title: Simplax: Enriching Discrete Diffusion Without Changing Its Noise
hook: Discrete diffusion is boxed in by its corruption kernel. Simplax bolts a continuous simplex variable onto each noisy token — richer training signal, same underlying categorical process.

title: StyleGAN: Controllable Image Synthesis
hook: A GAN that generates photorealistic faces of people who don't exist — and lets you dial features at different scales, from face shape down to freckles.

title: Humanity's Last Exam
hook: Humanity's Last Exam is a 3,000-question expert benchmark built to be the hardest closed-ended test there is — designed to outlast frontier models as MMLU saturated.

title: The Kernel Trick
hook: Instead of explicitly mapping data into a high-dimensional space, just define a function that computes similarities as if you had - and you get nonlinear learning for free.

title: Don't Resample — Rewind to the Bad Token
hook: Resampling after a failure throws away the reasoning that was still correct. TTEL finds the token where things went wrong and branches from there — same pass@64, half the tokens.

title: Agent Memory Poisoning Beats Content Screening
hook: Poison 1.2% of an agent's long-term memory with plain false sentences and accuracy falls from 0.85 to 0.30 — while an injection screener catches literally none of them.

title: Making Distillation Cheap: Offline Top-K Logits and a Fused Chunked KL Loss
hook: You don't need the teacher in memory. Cache its top-K logits once, then train the student against the cache — same loss, ~29% faster per step, and 4x the context on one GPU.

title: SHAPER: Adapting Embodied Agents by Evolving Skills and Harness, Not Weights
hook: When a robot agent fails in a new environment, the reflex is to fine-tune. SHAPER freezes the model and instead evolves the skills and harness wrapped around it — no data, no rewards, no training run.

title: Attractor States Emerge in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
hook: Let two LLMs debate long enough and one model's style pulls the other toward it — Claude Haiku drags partners into its own habits, while GPT-4.1 nano is easily swayed.

title: Regularization: Ridge & Lasso
