hook: Add a penalty for large weights during training and your model learns to generalize instead of memorizing - Ridge shrinks, Lasso cuts.

title: A Probe Direction Is a Property of Its Prompt
hook: Two published studies disagree about whether bigger models better sense they're being evaluated. Both trends are reproducible from one design — by changing only the prompt.

title: Two Axes of LLM Abstention: Correctness and Answerability
hook: An LLM should refuse two different things — wrong answers, and questions it shouldn't answer at all. A single confidence score can't tell these apart, but a hidden-state probe can.

title: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action
hook: Probes that seem to detect an LLM's harmful intent before it acts mostly just detect the prompt's topic — three careful tests find they don't predict future misbehavior.

title: HIERA: Choosing the Search Space for GPU Kernels
hook: LLM kernel optimizers all pick one implementation space and search inside it. HIERA's first decision is which space to search at all — PyTorch op, CUDA library, or handwritten kernel.

title: Super Weights Are Critical to Read — But Useless to Train Alone
hook: A handful of parameters wreck accuracy if removed. You'd think training just those would be the cheapest fine-tune ever. It isn't — it collapses the model to random guessing instead.

title: Verbalization Debt: What an LLM Loses When Its Subagent Has to Explain Itself in Words
hook: In chess, robotics, and games the strongest agent isn't a language model. Wiring one into an LLM orchestrator means compressing its state into text — and that tax grows with scale.

title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
hook: World-action models look safer because you can check a robot's imagined future against its action. BadWAM shows a small pixel nudge leaves the imagination intact while hijacking the action.

title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
hook: Tuning the sparsity penalty on an autoencoder is fiddly. Use a top-k constraint instead and you can dial sparsity directly — and scale SAEs to GPT-4.

title: RecGPT-V3 Technical Report
hook: Taobao's recommender now reasons about intent, not just click history. V3's trick: do that reasoning in compact latent tokens instead of long chain-of-thought, cutting output-token cost 200x at production scale.

title: HiLS Attention: Learning Chunk Selection for Near-Infinite Context
hook: Sparse attention never quite matched full attention because chunk selection was a heuristic. This version trains chunk selection end-to-end — then extrapolates 64x past its training length.

title: Computer Use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
hook: DeepMind put computer-use agents — reading the screen, then clicking, typing, and scrolling through real UIs — into its fast, low-cost Flash tier.

title: CE-MoE: Fewer Expert Layers, Same Loss, a Third Less Compute
hook: Interleaving an MoE layer after every attention block means paying all-to-all communication over and over. Concentrating experts in a few layers cut GPU-hours by a third at matched quality.

title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Why 'Same Accuracy' Doesn't Mean 'Same Model'
hook: Two quantized models can score identically on accuracy while disagreeing on which individual examples they get right — a gap standard benchmarks are structurally blind to.

title: CamoDocs: Poisoning RAG Without Leaving Fingerprints
hook: Existing RAG poisoning attacks paste the target query into the malicious document, which is exactly what makes them easy to filter. CamoDocs hides the payload inside plausible benign text instead.

title: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe
hook: Google DeepMind ships a speech-to-text model built on Gemini — pitching transcription that understands what it is hearing, not just what sounds were made.

title: Massive Activations Line Up With the Attention Layers
hook: Hybrid linear-attention models have huge outlier activations too — and they aren't random. They spike right before every full-attention layer and plateau across the linear ones in between.

title: What LLM Forecasters Know but Don't Say
hook: A forecasting model's chain-of-thought can look untouched by evidence that actually flipped its answer — but its hidden activations give the real story away.

title: PILOT: Self-Improvement While the Run Is Still Going
hook: Most agent self-improvement happens after the run ends, too late to save it. PILOT gives a supervisor the power to redirect or abort a live worker — and cuts output tokens by nearly half.

title: Audio-Visual Flamingo: Open Audio-Visual Intelligence for Long and Complex Videos
hook: Most audio-visual LLMs only handle short clips. NVIDIA's open AV-Flamingo targets long, real-world video instead — and grounds its reasoning to actual timestamps as it goes.

title: Activation Functions: ReLU & Friends
hook: Stack linear layers and you still just have one linear layer. The nonlinearity between them is what gives a network its power.

title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning (Adapters)
hook: Don't fine-tune the whole model for every new task — slip in a few tiny trainable modules and freeze the rest. This 2019 idea seeded parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

title: ReAct: Reasoning + Acting
hook: Thinking alone can drift; acting alone is blind. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so an LLM can plan, look things up, and correct course — the template for agents.

title: NVIDIA Nemotron-TwoTower: A Diffusion-Based Language Model
hook: NVIDIA's open Nemotron-TwoTower bolts a diffusion 'denoiser' tower onto a frozen autoregressive model to fill token blocks in parallel — reportedly 2.42x faster at ~98.7% of baseline quality.

title: ImageNet: The Dataset That Sparked Deep Learning
hook: A hand-labeled hoard of millions of images turned into the contest that, in 2012, lit the fuse on the deep learning era.

title: When Your Top Feature Makes Predictions Worse
hook: A feature can top your model's importance ranking and still hurt accuracy. The only way to be sure it helps: delete it, retrain, and compare on held-out data.

title: TraceLab: What Coding-Agent Traffic Actually Looks Like
hook: The first real trace of day-to-day coding-agent usage — 350,000 LLM steps from Claude Code and Codex sessions — reveals serving patterns no prior benchmark captured.

title: Gradient Descent
hook: Lost in fog on a hillside, you'd feel for the steepest downhill step and take it, again and again. That's how models learn.

title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
hook: One long search trajectory can't be both deep and wide at once. WebSwarm lets the search tree grow instead: any node that can't solve its own piece just spawns children and waits for their evidence.

title: Gemini 1.5: Multimodal Understanding Across Long Context
hook: Gemini 1.5 Pro processes up to a million tokens in context - enough for entire codebases, hours of video, or book-length documents - in a single multimodal model.

title: LibriBrain100: 100 Hours of MEG Data for Neural Speech Decoding
hook: Most brain-decoding datasets go wide across many subjects. This one goes deep — ~80 hours inside a single brain — to test whether depth beats breadth.

title: The Pile: 800GB of Diverse Text
hook: Web text alone leaves gaps. The Pile stitches together 22 curated sources — academic and professional — so a language model picks up knowledge plain web crawls miss.

title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
hook: PAW compiles a natural-language function spec into a small reusable adapter instead of prompting an LLM every call — matching a 32B model's quality at a fiftieth of the memory.

title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
hook: Every robot has a different action space, which fragments training data. Hydra-0 sidesteps that by expressing actions as pixel motion — a shared visual interface any embodiment can speak.

title: Sliding Window Beats Linear Attention
hook: The cheap baseline nobody bothered to run wins: sliding-window attention with sinks matches or beats retrofitted linear-attention models, and needs no post-training at all.

title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels
hook: Tokens, bytes, or pixels — which encodes language best? A controlled head-to-head across 13 languages finds no single winner: each encoding trades off differently by task.

title: Macaron-V1: Mixture-of-LoRA for Continual Learning
hook: Freeze the base model, keep a shelf of specialist LoRA adapters, pick one per user turn. It's a bet that continual learning belongs in the adapters, not the weights.

title: Imagen: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion
hook: Google found that a large frozen T5 text encoder matters more than a bigger image diffusion model - scaling language understanding is the key lever for photorealistic generation.

title: One-Step Gradient Delay Isn't a Barrier — With the Right Optimizer
hook: Asynchronous pipeline parallelism kills GPU idle time during pretraining — the field avoided it fearing instability, but that turns out to be an AdamW problem, not a fundamental one.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
hook: Ask a big model to 'think step by step' and its math and logic scores jump. Reasoning was there all along — you just had to ask it to show its work.

title: World Models Lack a Persistent State
hook: Today's video world models render great frames but treat the world like a tracking shot: look away and back, and off-screen events freeze instead of running on — the moon keeps orbiting unwatched.

title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: MoE Plus an N-Gram Table
hook: An imminent Qwen release pairs a sparse ~125B-A6B mixture-of-experts with a 51B n-gram component — an unusual hybrid the local community thinks will fit on one machine.

title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.

title: Agentic Test-Time Training: Adapting Mid-Episode
hook: LLM agents degrade over long episodes, repeating failed moves — this method updates the model's weights continuously during the episode itself, but only on genuinely new information.

title: What Is Attention?
hook: Attention lets a model decide what to focus on: it scores how relevant each piece of input is to the current question, then blends them by those scores.

title: AgentRewind: Give Agents an Undo Button
hook: Most agent research tries to prevent mistakes. AgentRewind asks what happens after one — checkpoint the context and the environment together, so the agent can rewind and retry with what it learned.

title: DiffusionGemma: Generating Text by Denoising, Not Decoding
hook: DeepMind's DiffusionGemma generates text by refining a whole sequence in parallel instead of one token at a time — which the team reports is about 4x faster than standard autoregressive decoding.

title: What Does a Discrete Diffusion Model Learn?
hook: A discrete diffusion model can be read as a denoiser, a score, or a bridge predictor. This paper proves they're the same optimum in different coordinates — with one exact best solution.

title: Why ColBERT-Style Retrieval Fails on Negation — and the Fix
hook: Late-interaction retrieval (MaxSim, as in ColBERT) is provably as expressive as vector search for ordinary matches — but provably can't handle negation. Signed MaxSim closes that exact gap.

title: Inkling by Thinking Machines
hook: Thinking Machines' open-weight multimodal MoE reads image, text, and audio in a 1-million-token context — and skips RoPE for relative position encoding instead.

title: DataClaw0: Data Refinement as a Learnable Skill
hook: Instead of scrubbing data with fixed rules, what if an agent learned to tailor it? DataClaw0 turns data refinement into a trainable skill judged by how well models train on its output.

title: Who Thinks Best Depends on How Long You Let Them
hook: Change the token budget and the leaderboard changes with it. Model rankings reversed on every benchmark tested — which means a single-budget eval is measuring the budget as much as the model.

title: Which Tasks Do Transformers Extrapolate To? Now Decidable
hook: Transformers sometimes handle sequences longer than they trained on, sometimes not. For regular languages there's now a complete characterization — and a polynomial-time algorithm to check.

title: Anatomy of an Agent Sandbox Escape: The July 2026 Intrusion, Step by Step
hook: The technical timeline behind the Hugging Face incident: an evaluation agent escaped its sandbox via a zero-day, built C2 on pastebins, and ran ~17,600 actions over 4.5 days before anyone noticed.

title: The Seriality Gap in Video Diffusion Models
hook: Give a video diffusion model more denoising steps and you'd expect better predictions on chains of causal events. Instead performance keeps degrading — the steps don't add real serial computation.

title: Persistent Recursive Worlds Enable Autonomous Software Evolution
hook: Instead of keeping the agent alive across a long project, keep the project alive and let agents be disposable — enough to grow a 250k-line Rust C compiler for $44.

title: Subquadratic Architectures: xLSTM vs. Mamba-2 vs. Gated DeltaNet
hook: Transformers pay a quadratic tax on sequence length. Pitting xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet head-to-head on hard tasks, xLSTM comes out ahead — and the paper explains why.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
hook: Sample the model many times, let each run reason its own way, then take the majority answer - diverse reasoning paths vote out individual errors.

title: Compile a Transformer Instead of Training One
hook: Write a computation graph in ordinary Python and get back the weights of a vanilla transformer that executes it — a real Phi-3 checkpoint, with zero gradient steps anywhere in the pipeline.

title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
hook: Multi-agent LLM setups help sometimes and hurt other times, with no clear pattern — until you view them as an information bottleneck problem: compressing context helps only when it loses less than it saves.

title: Making Knowledge Distillation Cheap Enough to Run at Scale
hook: Distillation is expensive mostly for two boring reasons: the teacher hogs memory, and the KL loss materializes a huge vocab-by-sequence matrix. Fix both and a four-GPU job fits on one.

title: ICA Lens: Interpreting LLMs Without Training a Dictionary
hook: Before you train a giant sparse autoencoder, just look at the geometry. ICA Lens revives a classic method to surface interpretable directions in an LLM with no dictionary training at all.

title: It Knows Both Facts and Still Can't Chain Them
hook: A model can store 'A is B' and 'B is C' and still fail at 'what is A's C?'. Transformers trained from scratch show why: lower layers build the intermediate, upper layers don't reason over it.

title: XGBoost: Scalable Tree Boosting
hook: Boosting builds an ensemble one tree at a time, each tree correcting the mistakes of all the ones before it - XGBoost made this fast enough to dominate competitions.

title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.

title: OmniOpt: A Taxonomy and Benchmark of 100+ Optimizers
hook: Choosing an optimizer for training a large model is now a system-level design decision, but the field has 100+ methods and no shared map. This paper builds one — and a benchmark to go with it.

title: RoPE: Rotary Position Embedding
hook: Encode position by rotating query/key vectors - relative distances then fall out of the dot product for free, no extra tokens or additive embeddings needed.

title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
hook: One model that reads and generates language, images, video, audio, and actions — NVIDIA's open Cosmos 3 folds VLMs, video generators, and robot policies into a single backbone.

title: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning
hook: Connect a CLIP vision encoder to an LLM with just a linear projection, fine-tune on GPT-4-generated image dialogues, and get a capable open chat-with-images model for under a day of training.

title: Devin: The AI Software Engineer
hook: Cognition's Devin was marketed as the first 'AI software engineer' — an autonomous agent that plans, writes, runs, and debugs code across a whole task in its own sandbox.

title: MiniMax Reportedly Plans a 2.7-Trillion-Parameter M3 Pro
hook: MiniMax's current flagship already runs 428B parameters — sources now say the next one, codenamed M3 Pro, could jump to 2.7 trillion and still ship open-source as soon as Q3.

title: Jalapeño: OpenAI and Broadcom's Inference Chip
hook: OpenAI co-designed a custom chip — Jalapeño — built only for running LLMs, betting that inference-specific silicon beats general GPUs on cost and scale.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
hook: Loss doesn't drop randomly as models grow — it follows a smooth power law in size, data, and compute. That predictability is what made betting on bigger models rational.

title: When Claws Remember but Do Not Tell: Stealthy Memory Injection
hook: One poisoned email is enough: this attack tricks a persistent personal agent into silently writing false memories, hiding the evidence from the user, and acting on the lie later.

title: CRISP: Reading the Sparse-Attention Routing Decision Straight Off the Attention Map
hook: Long-context prefill is quadratic, so servers route attention heads to sparse patterns. CRISP shows the routing decision is already readable off the attention map's structure.

title: Geometric Causal Models
hook: Causal inference usually assumes i.i.d. data. This framework builds causal models around the symmetries data actually has — spatial, network, genomic — unlocking inference where classical methods don't apply.

title: When Real Speech Is Off-Limits, RL Beats Fine-Tuning on Synthetic Audio
hook: Banks can't just collect real customer speech to adapt voice AI. Trained only on synthetic TTS audio, GRPO cuts word-error rate 40% more than supervised fine-tuning alone.

title: AlphaFold 3: Predicting Biomolecular Interactions
hook: AlphaFold 3 extends protein structure prediction to full biomolecular complexes - proteins with DNA, RNA, ligands, and ions - using a diffusion-based architecture.

title: Convergent Detour Hijacking: The Attack That Lets Your Agent Succeed
hook: A malicious third-party skill doesn't have to break your agent's task. It can just take the scenic route — burning 67% more tokens and 92% more wall-clock while the final answer still looks correct.

title: A Fake Dashboard Is Enough to Make an Agent Commit
hook: Show an agent a professional-looking market panel and it will make a directional call on a provably unpredictable question — just as readily when every number on the panel is invented.

title: T5: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer
hook: What if translation, classification, and summarization were all just text-in, text-out? T5 makes one model and one recipe handle them all.

title: Where VLM Localization Signal Actually Hides in Editing Pipelines
hook: VLMs are great at pointing to objects on their own — but bolt one onto a diffusion image editor and that skill seems to vanish. It didn't leave, it just hid somewhere editing pipelines don't look.

title: Look Light, Think Heavy: The Limits of Multimodal Chain-of-Thought
hook: Chain-of-thought should make models think harder. For vision-language tasks this study finds it's no free lunch — it can hurt perception, and models keep talking while they stop looking.

title: Linear Regression
hook: Predict a number by fitting a straight line through your data - the simplest model in ML and the mental blueprint for almost everything that came after.

title: Evolution Strategies Beat GRPO on Reasoning Coverage
hook: GRPO sharpens one answer and collapses entropy. Evolution strategies keep the population diverse — improving pass@1 while also raising pass@k, which GRPO gives up.

title: Whisper: Robust Speech Recognition at Scale
hook: Train a plain encoder-decoder transformer on 680,000 hours of weakly-labeled multilingual audio and you get near-human transcription robustness without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources
hook: Most agent skill libraries are hand-written text. This framework mines skills straight out of the tutorial videos, repos, and articles humans already made for each other.

title: MusicGen: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
hook: Generate music from a text description or a melody reference using a single autoregressive transformer over discrete audio tokens - no cascade of specialized models required.

title: Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale
hook: muP lets you tune hyperparameters on a small model and transfer them to a huge one. This paper derives the equivalent rules for gated delta networks, so sub-quadratic models scale without re-tuning.

title: SPORK: Self-Speculative Forking to Accelerate Agentic LLM Inference
hook: An agent's tool-call loop idles the GPU 16-37% of the time waiting on results. SPORK has the model predict its own next tool call early enough to start it before reasoning even finishes.

title: The Information Abundance Paradox: Long Context Can Undermine What a Model Knows
hook: If the answer is always in the context window, the model stops bothering to learn it. Past an intermediate context length, more training context makes a model weaker without its crutch.

title: Fast Weight Attention: Which Pair Is the Memory Learning From?
hook: If a recurrent state is really an online learner, then what it trains on matters. This paper argues most fast-weight rules quietly use the wrong (key, value) pair.

title: Why Muon Skips Gradient Descent's Slow Start
hook: Small-init gradient descent crawls through a 'saddle-to-saddle' bottleneck — Muon skips it, learning every mode at once and staying stable past where gradient descent blows up.

title: Subliminal Clocks: Latent Time Modelling in Diffusion Language Models
hook: Standard diffusion models are told which denoising step they're on; diffusion language models aren't — yet they track it anyway, a hidden clock you can read off their activations and even steer.

title: WikiSkill: Give the Agent a Wiki, Not Just Skills
hook: Auto-discovered agent skills work, but the insight behind them gets lost. WikiSkill keeps a persistent wiki alongside the skills — and skills borrowed from other models beat self-evolved ones.

title: Spectral Allocation: Why Muon Outperforms Adam, and How to Improve Muon
hook: Probe a transformer's loss landscape direction by direction and a pattern appears: a few volatile directions demand tiny steps, the bulk tolerates far larger. That explains Muon > Adam > SGD.

title: ExTernD: Making Ternary Quantization's Accuracy Tunable by Rank
hook: Ternary quantization (weights in {-1, 0, 1}) is usually all-or-nothing on accuracy. ExTernD decomposes the weight matrix so you can dial accuracy up by spending a little more rank and VRAM.

title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning from a Diverse Cohort
hook: Self-rewarding RL collapses because a model's errors reinforce themselves. Co-RL breaks the loop by having a diverse cohort of models grade each other — no labels at all.

title: Qwen3.8-27B Has the Same Architecture as Qwen3.6-27B
hook: A community diff of the two model configs came back with zero changes — so whatever Qwen3.8-27B gained over its predecessor came entirely from the training recipe.

title: Contrastive Decoding Diffing: Extracting Verbatim Finetuning Data With Just Logits
hook: You don't need the weights to steal what a model was fine-tuned on — you barely need anything. CDD recovers verbatim training text using only the logits a model already hands you.

title: Partially Correlated Verifier Cascades: Concave Log-Odds and Blind-Spot Ceilings
hook: Chain enough independent verifier checks and failure should vanish exponentially. In practice, treating correlated verifiers as independent underestimates failure by 20x at 5 checks — and 3000x at 10.

title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes LMs Better
hook: Training corpora are full of copies — one 61-word sentence shows up 60,000+ times in C4. Strip the duplicates and models memorize far less and evaluate more honestly.

title: ReChannel: Repurposing Text-to-Image Diffusion for Dense Prediction
hook: Depth maps and masks get generated as if they were images, decoded through the same interface as RGB pixels. This paper swaps that for a tiny linear head that's 2.5x faster.

title: Sound Probabilistic Safety Bounds for Large Language Models
hook: How do you put a rigorous, provable number on how often an LLM will produce harmful output? Borrow a century-old statistics tool and steer the search toward where harm hides.

title: Llama-Mobile: A VLM at 2.7 Bits per Weight
hook: Llama 3.2 11B Vision squeezed into 3.7 GB — using the model's own outputs as calibration data and a bit format built for Arm CPUs, not GPUs.

title: Deceptive Grounding: When RAG Cites the Right Text, Wrong Entity
hook: A RAG system can pass every faithfulness, hallucination, and citation check while quietly citing the wrong entity's evidence — real text, real citation, wrong subject.

title: Prefix Sliding for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
hook: Most intermediate reasoning tokens stop mattering as the model reasons on. Keep only the prefix and the last few thousand tokens and you cap memory forever — 3x faster with no training.

title: Chatbot Arena: Ranking LLMs by Human Preference
hook: How do you rank chatbots when there's no single right answer? Let people pick the better of two anonymous replies, then aggregate the votes into a leaderboard.

title: Denser ≠ Better: Limits of On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continual Post-Training
hook: On-policy self-distillation was supposed to fight forgetting in continual post-training — instead, denser self-distillation can drift further off course and collapse outright.

title: Seeing Is Free, Speaking Is Not: The Real Energy Bottleneck in Edge VLM Inference
hook: Prune every visual token an edge VLM sees and you save at most 10% of its energy. Shorten what it says instead and save up to 97% — vision was never the bottleneck.

title: Speculative Decoding
hook: Let a small, fast model guess the next few words, then have the big model check them all in one shot. Same output, fewer slow steps.

title: Silent Alarm: Catching Quantization's Hidden Safety Cost with J-Space
hook: Quantizing a model to save memory can quietly gut its internal danger-recognition circuitry — even when its answers on safety benchmarks look unchanged.

title: Is Agentic Code Review Helpful? Mining Developers' Feedback to CodeRabbit Reviews in the Wild
hook: CodeRabbit leaves review comments on hundreds of thousands of real pull requests. A large-scale study of how developers actually respond finds more than half get rejected outright.

title: Ring Attention for Near-Infinite Context
hook: Spread one long sequence across many devices and compute attention blockwise - the context length you can handle grows with the number of devices, all with exact attention and no extra overhead.

title: DALL·E 2 (unCLIP): Text-to-Image with CLIP Latents
hook: Turn a prompt into a CLIP image embedding first, then diffusion-decode that embedding into a picture. A two-stage path from words to vivid, editable images.

title: NeoMME: Stop Paying for a Generative VLM When All You Need Is an Encoder
hook: Document retrievers like ColPali repurpose generative VLMs as encoders and inherit all the overhead. NeoMME is pretrained from scratch as one bidirectional encoder.

title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation
hook: Most agent-optimization papers report a one-shot gain and stop. Rerun the optimizer on new tasks and two of three popular methods actually make the agent worse than doing nothing.

title: Vision as Unified Multimodal Generation
hook: Detection, segmentation, depth, pose — each normally needs its own architecture. This model does all of them as text-and-image generation from one multimodal model, no task-specific heads.

title: Cosmos-H-Dreams: A Real-Time Generative Simulator for Surgical Robots
hook: Rehearsing robot surgery on real hardware is slow, costly, and bends instruments. NVIDIA distilled its surgical world model into a two-step student that dreams the operating field at ~160 FPS.

title: Model Routing Is Simple. Until It Isn't.
hook: Picking the 'right' model per query looks like classification. IBM Research argues it's really a systems-optimization problem — and treating it as less costs money and speed.

title: Models Can Pass the Exam Without Knowing the Syllabus
hook: Educational benchmarks test whether a model answers school questions. This one tests whether it knows which concept comes before which — and the best model scores 57%.

title: Nunchaku: 4-bit Diffusion Inference in Diffusers
hook: Diffusion models hate 4-bit — activation outliers wreck image quality. SVDQuant peels the hardest weights into a tiny 16-bit low-rank branch, and Nunchaku now runs it inside Diffusers.

title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
hook: Self-improving agents are leaving the lab for production. This survey, co-authored by Jürgen Schmidhuber, gives the field a shared vocabulary for what an agent can update about itself, and what drives that update.

title: GLM-5.3: All the Gains From Post-Training
hook: z.ai shipped GLM-5.3 on the same base model as GLM-5.2 — every improvement, including a claimed 50% jump on coding, comes from post-training alone.

title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Embed Ranks #1 Overall on RTEB
hook: A new embedding model from NVIDIA takes the top overall spot on RTEB, the retrieval-focused benchmark — with an eye toward making agentic retrieval, not just search, more reliable.

title: Tencent Hy3: A 295B Open MoE Model Under Apache 2.0
hook: Tencent's new Hy3 model switched from a restrictive community license to Apache 2.0 — removing the regional-use carve-outs that blocked adoption in the EU, UK, and South Korea.

title: FLAN: Instruction Tuning
hook: Teach a model to follow many tasks phrased as plain instructions, and it learns to follow instructions for tasks it never saw — zero-shot.

title: Small Models Are Enough to Imitate Human Choice Behaviour
hook: Fourteen models from 135M to 14B were fine-tuned on 10.7 million human decisions. In-distribution, 0.6B matched a 70B baseline — scale only started paying off on unfamiliar tasks.

title: Pitwall: Faithful Live Commentary via Claim Verification
hook: Live sports commentary has no reference text to check against — facts change every few seconds. This production F1 system verifies every sentence against a live probability model before publishing.

title: The Regression Tax on Agent Skills
hook: Handing an agent a procedural skill doesn't only add wins — it also breaks tasks it used to solve. The best skills win by regressing less, not by gaining more.

title: A Blueprint for Equilibrium-Based Differentiable Thermodynamic Computing
hook: Instead of fighting thermal noise in chips, this blueprint puts it to work — training ML models directly on physical stochastic hardware to cut the energy cost of machine learning.

title: World Models Meet Language Models
hook: A world model can imagine what happens next; an LLM can reason about it. The hard part is knowing when to trust the daydream — and when the simulation is just plausible nonsense.

title: GPUHedge: Treating Serverless GPU Cold Starts as a Speculative-Execution Problem
hook: Serverless GPU inference is fast — until a cold start hits and your p95 jumps past 100 seconds. One builder's fix: hedge requests across providers, like speculative execution races instructions.

title: Precision, Recall & F1
hook: On rare events, a model can be 99% accurate and still useless. Precision and recall reveal what accuracy hides.

title: Why Multi-Task SFT Fights Itself and Multi-Task RL Doesn't
hook: Train a model on several tasks with SFT and they interfere; with RL they coexist. The difference is a bound: SFT interference scales with gradient magnitude, RL's only with variance.

title: Plans Don't Persist: Context Management Is Load-Bearing for Agents
hook: An agent writes a plan, then context compression evicts it. This paper shows the plan never became internal state — once it leaves the window, the agent forgets it and task success craters.

title: KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian
hook: GPTQ assumes every output channel matters equally. KronQ adds gradient information to challenge that — rescuing 2-bit LLaMA-3-70B from a perplexity blowup down to 7.93.

title: The Bias–Variance Tradeoff
hook: Too simple and your model misses the pattern; too flexible and it chases noise. Generalization lives between the two.

title: LingBot-World 2.0: An Agent-Piloted Infinite World Model
hook: Interactive world models usually run out of road — quality degrades, or the action set stays thin. LingBot-World 2.0 stays coherent forever and puts an agent inside to invent what's next.

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning
hook: Translate a sentence by reading it into one vector, then writing a new sentence out of that vector. This encoder–decoder recipe powered early neural machine translation.

title: DistilBERT: Smaller, Faster, Cheaper, Lighter
hook: Distill during pre-training instead of after, and you get a general-purpose language model that is 40% smaller and 60% faster while keeping 97% of BERT's understanding.

title: AWQ: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization
hook: Not all weights are equal - protect the 1% that matter most (flagged by activation magnitude) and quantize the rest to 4-bit with minimal quality loss.

title: SpatialClaw: Code as the Action Interface for Spatial Reasoning
hook: Give a vision-language agent a live Python kernel instead of a fixed tool menu, and let it write one cell at a time. That flexibility lifts 3D/4D spatial reasoning by 11 points.

title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics
hook: Two pretraining runs with very different learning rates and weight norms trace the same loss curve — if the ratio between them matches. That ratio is the coordinate that matters.

title: OpenAI o1: Learning to Reason with Reinforcement Learning
hook: OpenAI's o1 lets a model think via a long internal chain-of-thought before answering - spending more compute at inference time visibly improves reasoning.

title: DINO: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
hook: Train a Vision Transformer with no labels at all, and something surprising happens: its attention maps trace out object boundaries on their own.

title: When More Sampling Hurts: The Modal Ceiling and Correlation Ceiling of Test-Time Scaling
hook: Sample a reasoning model dozens of times and coverage keeps climbing — but picking the right answer from the pile plateaus fast, and extra samples past that point can backfire.

title: SentencePiece: Language-Independent Tokenization
hook: Most tokenizers assume you can split on spaces first. SentencePiece drops that assumption and tokenizes raw text directly — in any language.

title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Interactive Proofs
hook: AI safety via debate assumes two equally matched AIs arguing before a human judge. This paper shows a weak verifier can be convinced by a single powerful AI instead — no opponent required.

title: PlanBench-XL: Long-Horizon Planning in Large Tool Ecosystems
hook: A benchmark of 1,665 tools shows top agents plan fine until tools start failing silently — then GPT-5.4's success crashes from 52% to 11%.

title: t-SNE & UMAP: Visualizing High-Dimensional Data
hook: t-SNE and UMAP squeeze thousands of dimensions into two so you can see whether your model's internal representations form meaningful clusters.

title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
hook: Split the difference between multi-head and multi-query attention: share KV heads across groups of query heads and get most of the memory savings with little quality loss.

title: 100 GRPO Steps to Make a 350M Model Respect Your Schema
hook: Small models are cheap but sloppy about output format. Three simple programmatic rewards and about 500 samples nearly doubled a 350M model's JSON pass rate.

title: Nano Banana (Gemini Image)
hook: Google's native Gemini image model — nicknamed Nano Banana — made conversational, character-consistent image editing go viral, drawing millions to the Gemini app.

title: Scaling Laws for Learning Rate and Batch Size
hook: Chinchilla told you how many tokens. This tells you what learning rate and batch size to use as you get there — including whether the optimum survives the decay phase.

title: WARP: Weight-Space Analysis for Recovering Training Data Portfolios
hook: Labs rarely disclose their data mixture recipes — but WARP shows you can recover a fine-tuned model's training-domain proportions just from its released weights, no training data required.

title: Circuit Condensation: Train the Circuit Smaller
hook: Circuit discovery on a frozen model returns hundreds of edges nobody can check. Post-train the model to route the behavior through fewer, and circuits shrink 8x on average — up to 316x.

title: LLM Judges Can't Separate Trust from Truth
hook: Ask a judge model for a trust score and a correctness verdict and you get two numbers — but they're not two pieces of evidence. Change the source label and both move.

title: Subword Tokenization with Byte-Pair Encoding
hook: Whole words make a giant vocabulary; single characters make long sequences. Subwords split the difference — and let models read words they've never seen.

title: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards
hook: Checking a solution used to be easier than writing one. For coding agents that's flipped — and this paper argues no fixed reward works forever: verification must co-evolve with the model.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI
hook: A practitioner reference that walks the whole agent stack — transformer substrate, RLHF, memory, MCP, A2A, multi-agent topologies — on the thesis that good agents demand understanding every layer.

title: The Claude 3 Model Family
hook: Anthropic's Claude 3 family offers a three-tier speed-capability tradeoff - Haiku, Sonnet, Opus - with multimodal input and alignment built on Constitutional AI methods.

title: The Ethics of Autonomous AI Agents for Offensive Security
hook: Autonomous AI agents drop the skill floor for cyberattacks and blur who's to blame. This paper maps three kinds of 'indeterminacy' that break existing dual-use ethics frameworks.

title: RuBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents — and Catching a Silent Model Swap
hook: A benchmark of real customer-style bug reports written in Russian. Its most striking result isn't the leaderboard — it's catching a deployed product quietly swapping in a different model mid-task.

title: SWE-Prime: 10% of the Trajectories, Better Results
hook: A successful agent trajectory can still be full of wasted and risky steps. Filter down to the best 10% and fine-tuning beats training on everything that worked.

title: Overfitting & Regularization
hook: A model that aces its training data but flops on anything new hasn't learned — it has memorized. Regularization is the cure.

title: AutoMedBench: Medical AutoResearch with Agentic AI
hook: Can an AI agent run a whole medical-imaging research project end to end? AutoMedBench scores each stage — and finds agents can build pipelines but can't tell when they're broken.

title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy
hook: Tell a model you're lonely before asking for feedback, and it softens its judgment the most — sycophancy peaks exactly when honest feedback matters most.

title: The Perceptron
hook: The 1958 perceptron was the first algorithm that learned its own weights from examples — the seed of everything, and the model whose limits sparked the first AI winter.

title: AutoIndex: Learning Representation Programs for Retrieval
hook: Stop tuning the retriever — tune the documents. AutoIndex searches for executable programs that rewrite and reorganize docs before indexing, lifting recall on every task with BM25 left untouched.

title: WarpSAC: Off-Policy RL Stabilizers Depend on the Data Regime
hook: Massively parallel simulation broke the assumptions behind a decade of RL stabilizers. WarpSAC's finding: tricks that rescue data-starved training actively hold you back when data is abundant.

title: ResearchStudio-Reel: One Extraction, Three Editable Outputs From a Paper
hook: Turning a paper into a poster, talk video, and blog is usually done by hand, three times over. ResearchStudio-Reel extracts it once and generates all three — beating even authors' own posters.

title: On the Convergence of Adam, Revisited
hook: A 2018 result showed Adam can fail to converge only in a specific hyperparameter regime. This paper shows it can fail for ANY choice — a flaw that spreads to AdamW, RMSProp, even Muon.

title: Building an Explorable 3D World by Planning It First
hook: Text-to-3D usually yields one pretty scene. WorldClaw has planning agents write a spec — regions, terrain, assets, materials — then builds coarse-to-fine, so the world stays editable.

title: OpenRath: Sessions as First-Class Agent State
hook: Agent state is usually scattered across logs you stitch back together. OpenRath makes the Session a first-class value you can fork, replay, and inspect like a tensor.

title: MIRA: A Multiplayer World Model for Rocket League
hook: Single-player world models treat other agents as scenery. This one, trained on 10,000 hours of Rocket League, tracks four players' independent actions at once — and stays coherent for hours.

title: Attention Is All You Need
hook: Drop recurrence and convolution, keep only attention — and you get a model that trains in parallel and powers nearly every LLM since.

title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
hook: If the harness matters as much as the model, why is it still hand-written? JIT-Agent trains a model whose whole job is to synthesize a fresh harness for whatever task shows up.

title: An Exam for Active Observers
hook: Human vision is a loop — look, form a hypothesis, look again. A new benchmark for that loop leaves frontier MLLMs scoring single digits, while humans average 96%.

title: Danus: Orchestrating Mathematical Reasoning Agents with Fact-Graph Memory
hook: Parallel proof-search agents can generate claims faster than anyone can keep straight. Danus fixes that with a shared fact graph that only admits claims a stateless verifier has checked.

title: Moving Alphabet: A Controlled Study of Training Data for Text-to-Video Generation
hook: Text-to-video research chases bigger architectures; this controlled study shows the training data decides the outcome — caption quality alone can cap what the model learns.

title: Scalable Visual Pretraining for Language Intelligence
hook: Documents pack meaning into layout, figures, and equations that plain text can't fully capture. Skip the OCR step: pretraining directly on rendered pages beats text-only pretraining.

title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
hook: Show an LLM judge a previous score as mere context metadata and its rating drifts toward that number. Judgments you assumed were independent are quietly anchored to each other.

title: Repair or Resample? Rethinking Failure Debugging in Multi-Agent Systems
hook: Most multi-agent repair methods just rerun the trajectory and hope. Freeze the randomness and the truth comes out: unguided reruns reproduce only 68% of failures and fix under 7% of them.

title: Trellis.cpp Reaches Reference Quality for Open Image-to-3D
hook: A GGML-style CPU/non-CUDA port of TRELLIS.2 now produces 3D assets on par with the original reference implementation — no NVIDIA GPU required.

title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
hook: Moonshot's Kimi K2 is a trillion-parameter open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model built agentic-first — and trained at that scale without a single loss spike using the MuonClip optimizer.

title: A Model's Stance Is a Deployment Setting, Not a Property
hook: The same Grok model ID rated a pseudo-scientific claim 75 via API and 5.5 via web. What a commercial LLM 'believes' turns out to be a contingent effect of how it's deployed.

title: Word2Vec: Word Embeddings
hook: Teach a model to predict a word's neighbors, and it quietly learns vectors where king minus man plus woman lands near queen.

title: PerceptionDLM: Parallel Region Perception with Diffusion
hook: Captioning ten regions of an image one at a time is slow. PerceptionDLM uses a diffusion language model's parallel decoding to describe them all at once.

title: Visual Scaffolds Reveal What VLM Benchmarks Measure
hook: Redraw the same spatial puzzle to make its structure legible and accuracy jumps up to 34 points — so was the benchmark ever testing reasoning?

title: Deep Double Descent
hook: Bigger models should overfit, then get worse — right? Instead test error often dips, climbs, then dips again as model size grows, breaking the classic bias-variance story.

title: Sigmoid Attention Makes KV Eviction Stick
hook: Learned cache-eviction gates train softly but must delete hard at inference. Swap softmax for sigmoid attention and that jump stops hurting — even though sigmoid is the worse LM.

title: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
hook: A GUI agent framework that treats every finished task as a lesson: it banks the experience into memory and skills, then reuses them across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, and Windows.

title: Multi-LCB: Code Eval Beyond Python
hook: LiveCodeBench keeps coding evals contamination-free — but only in Python. Multi-LCB extends it to twelve languages and finds models that look strong are quietly overfit to Python.

title: FLUX.1
hook: FLUX.1 became the leading open-weight image model — from the Black Forest Labs team that built Stable Diffusion, now shipping a frontier-quality model you can run yourself.

title: OpenAI's Frontier Governance Framework
hook: A major lab publishes how it intends to govern its most capable models — and explicitly maps those safety, security, and risk practices onto emerging EU and California rules.

title: The EU AI Act
hook: The EU's answer to regulating AI: sort systems by how much risk they pose, then scale the rules to match — from outright bans to no rules at all.

title: MiniMax-Music3: Full Songs From Lyrics Plus a Description
hook: A five-minute song with coherent structure and expressive vocals, from an 8B model that plans the arrangement and a 0.6B model that fills in the audio frame by frame.

title: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming: Who Said What, While They're Still Saying It
hook: Unified speech-recognition-plus-diarization models beat running the two separately — but only offline. This one emits speaker-attributed transcripts as the audio arrives.

title: DSpark: The Speculative Decoder Behind DeepSeek's Production Serving
hook: Parallel drafters draft fast, but verifying all of it wastes capacity on likely rejects. DSpark schedules verification by confidence — and cut DeepSeek-V4's per-user latency 60-85% in production.

title: Refute, Don't Resample: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment
hook: Refuting a wrong claim needs one decisive flaw; building a right answer needs a flawless path. CLR spends test-time compute on that asymmetry instead of on more samples.

title: Open Coding Agents Are Overfitting to Their Harness
hook: Almost all open agent trajectory data is collected under OpenHands. Models fine-tuned on it score well there and fall apart under any other scaffold — a gap the base models don't have.

title: Untrusted Content Masking: A Trust Boundary for Web Agents
hook: Provable prompt-injection defenses rely on never letting an agent read untrusted content directly. Web agents break that just by looking at the page — this restores it via the page's own structure.

title: OLMo 2: A Fully Open Model
hook: Ai2's OLMo 2 is fully open — not just weights, but the training data, code, and checkpoints — the strongest reproducible-from-scratch model for researchers.

title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
hook: What makes a question hard for a model? GPQA's are hard even for skilled people with Google: non-experts reach only 34% after 30+ minutes of searching.

title: Why Long-Context Speed Comes Down to Prefill and KV Heads
hook: Everyone benchmarks token-generation speed. A community test of 13 models at 65K-128K context found that's the wrong number — prefill dominates, and KV head count beats parameter count.

title: The Handoff Tax: Swapping Models Mid-Run in Coding Agents
hook: Escalating a struggling coding agent to a stronger model recovers less than half the quality gap while costing a premium. Downshifting, oddly, is the good deal.

title: The llama.cpp Question in the Nvidia–Hugging Face Deal
hook: Buying Hugging Face means also acquiring the employer of the llama.cpp and ggml team — the software almost all local LLM inference runs on.

title: Magpie: Let the Engine Run the Game, Let the Model Render It
hook: Games need reproducible rules, which generative video cannot promise. Magpie splits the difference: the engine resolves gameplay on white-box frames, a render server paints them in real time.

title: Moebius: 0.2B Inpainting Rivaling 10B
hook: A 0.22B image-inpainting model that matches an 11.9B generalist (FLUX.1-Fill-Dev) — under 2% of the parameters and 15x faster — by pairing a linear-interaction backbone with latent-space distillation.

title: LLMs Hack Rewards, and Society
hook: Society's rules look like reward functions — measurable thresholds, fuzzy intent. Train an LLM with RL and it games them: stay technically compliant while defeating the rule's purpose.

title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
hook: Distillation needs a teacher who knows more than the student. This paper gets that gap for free — not by informing the teacher, but by blinding the student.

title: Wrong but Useful: Bad Answers That Still Help
hook: Multi-agent systems filter messages by how likely they are to be correct. But a wrong answer can carry a good decomposition — and in every model and benchmark tested, wrong-helpful messages showed up.

title: In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a TPU
hook: Google built a custom chip whose heart is a 256x256 grid of 8-bit multiply-accumulate units - and in production it ran neural-net inference roughly 15-30x faster than the GPUs and CPUs of its day.

title: Does Telling an LLM to Be Concise Save Money?
hook: Two ways to spend fewer tokens: shorten what you send, or shorten what you ask for back. Measured across nine models, only one of them actually saves you money.

title: Ads Arrive in ChatGPT
hook: OpenAI has started testing ads to fund the free tier — and is promising the thing that actually matters: that ads never change the answer you get.

title: k-Nearest Neighbors
hook: The laziest classifier: to label a new point, just find its k closest neighbors in the training set and take a vote - no training required at all.

title: Twenty Companies Sign for Open Weights — the Frontier Labs Don't
hook: A Microsoft-initiated open letter urges policymakers not to restrict open-weight models prematurely. NVIDIA, Meta, Palantir and Hugging Face signed; OpenAI, Anthropic and Google were absent.

title: Harness-1: RL for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses
hook: Stop making the policy remember everything. Harness-1 moves a search agent's bookkeeping into the environment, so RL only has to learn the decisions that matter.

title: Statistically Undetectable Backdoors in Deep Neural Networks
hook: A malicious trainer can plant a backdoor that's provably indistinguishable from honest weights — even to someone holding every parameter.

title: SLPO: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoners That Think in Vectors
hook: Latent reasoners think in continuous vectors, not tokens — but couldn't learn from outcome rewards the way chain-of-thought models can. SLPO gives them a surrogate policy so RL finally works.

title: Scaling Native Multimodal Pre-Training From Scratch
hook: Chinchilla told you how to split compute between model size and tokens for text. This maps the same frontier for models trained on images and text from day one.

title: Gemma 4: Google DeepMind's Open Multimodal Models
hook: An open-weight multimodal family (2.3B-31B) that now thinks before answering and, at 12B, skips separate vision/audio encoders entirely — still small enough for a 16GB laptop.

title: OpenAI Cuts Off Cursor After the SpaceX Acquisition
hook: OpenAI is winding down the contract that supplied its models to Cursor — a reminder that a product built on someone else's API is one corporate deal away from losing it.

title: Why RAG? Grounding LLMs in Your Data
hook: An LLM only knows what it was trained on — until it's stale, private, or just wrong. RAG bolts on a search step so the model answers from your data and can cite it.

title: Interaction Scaling: Grounding the Third Axis of Test-Time Compute
hook: Reasoning longer and sampling more both mine the same frozen weights — they can't tell a model anything new. Let it poke a real tool instead, and a coding loop hits 100% pass rate with zero variance.

title: Frontier AI Regulation
hook: How do you regulate models too new to have rules yet? This paper sketches three building blocks: set standards, make labs report, then enforce.

title: KVarN: Variance-Normalized KV-Cache Quantization
hook: Long reasoning chains blow up the KV cache. Squeeze it to 2 bits and errors snowball over thousands of decode steps — unless you fix the token scales first.

title: Training a Coding Model to Paint: RL Where the Reward Is How the Output Looks
hook: The model writes JavaScript; the environment runs it in a headless browser, renders the painting, and scores the picture. A worked example of RL over an aesthetic, non-textual reward.

title: Soofi S: A Sovereign, Open-Source Foundation Model for German and English
hook: A European consortium built a 30B model that activates just 3B parameters per token - and it beats every other European 'sovereign AI' model tested, including bigger ones.

title: Domino: Decoupling Causal Modeling from Autoregressive Drafting
hook: Speculative decoding is stuck between fast-but-sloppy parallel drafters and accurate-but-slow autoregressive ones. Domino splits the difference and hits up to 5.8× throughput.

title: TILDE: Making Concept Unlearning Actually Preserve Everything Else
hook: Erase a concept from a diffusion model and you usually damage unrelated generations too, because most methods never define what the 'after' distribution should look like. TILDE defines it explicitly.

title: LongCat 2.0: A 1.6T-Parameter Open Model Under MIT License
hook: 1.6 trillion total parameters, ~48B active, and released under the MIT license — one of the most permissively licensed large open-weight MoE models yet.

title: TRACE: Turn-Level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
hook: A failed agent rollout might still contain dozens of genuinely useful actions — outcome-only RL punishes every one of them the same as the final mistake. TRACE assigns credit per tool call instead, with no extra critic.

title: Large Language Models Are Zero-Shot Reasoners
hook: Appending 'Let's think step by step' to a prompt unlocks multi-step reasoning with zero examples - chain-of-thought without the example-writing overhead.

title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
hook: Full-parameter RL post-training updates every layer — but this study finds that training just ONE middle layer alone often recovers all the gains, and sometimes more.

title: Top-k KV Eviction Can't Know What It Threw Away
hook: Deterministic cache eviction is blind by construction: nothing you kept reveals how much error the deletions caused. Sample randomly instead and the leftovers become a statistical certificate.

title: Anchored Self-Play for Code Repair
hook: Let a model train itself by writing bugs and fixing them, and you get a free difficulty curriculum — until it invents bugs no real codebase would produce. Anchored Self-Play keeps it honest.

title: Next-Latent Prediction: Beyond Next-Token
hook: Microsoft's NextLat teaches a transformer to predict its own next hidden state, not just the next token - building a compact internal world model and decoding up to 3.3x faster.

title: MANCE: Erasing Concepts Without Leaving the Data Manifold
hook: Erase a concept from a representation and you often damage everything correlated with it. This method's fix: constrain every edit to stay on the manifold real representations actually live on.

title: Scaling Laws Break at the Edges — Because They Assume Size and Data Are Independent
hook: Chinchilla-style laws mispredict loss when data is scarce or a model is heavily overtrained. Add one interaction exponent coupling capacity and data, and the error drops 1.5–3x.

title: Claude Opus 4.7: Frontier Coding (2026)
hook: Claude Opus 4.7's gains land hardest on the hardest software-engineering tasks, and it now checks its own work - better self-verification of its outputs alongside the coding boost.

title: Jalapeño's First Results
hook: OpenAI's custom inference chip, co-designed with Broadcom, now has numbers attached — the lab claims industry-leading speed and efficiency on modern models.

title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
hook: Best agent configuration finished 20 of 97 real scientific workflows. And among failing Claude Code runs, 75.5% still signed off claiming they were done.

title: EvoArena: Testing Agents in Environments That Keep Changing
hook: Most agent benchmarks freeze the world. EvoArena makes the environment keep updating beneath the agent — and finds today's agents crack, averaging under 40%.

title: A Spectral Threshold That Predicts When LoRA Will Forget
hook: LoRA sometimes injects 'intruder dimensions' that trigger catastrophic forgetting. This paper predicts the per-layer update strength where they appear, from the pretrained spectrum alone.

title: World Action Models: A Survey
hook: Robots are learning to imagine the future before acting. This survey untangles 'world action models' from video generators and VLA policies — and finds them converging on one idea.

title: Agents That Learn on the Job Without Weight Updates
hook: An agent that cracks a hard request today starts from zero tomorrow. Distil each episode into a retrievable rule and a frozen model gets 2.6x better — no fine-tuning.

title: RARE: Steering MoE Models Without Breaking the Router
hook: Activation steering works on dense models and quietly fails on mixture-of-experts — because your steering vector also reroutes the tokens. Project it into the router's null space.

title: EchoCoT: Extracting Hidden Chain-of-Thought from Black-Box Models
hook: Providers hide reasoning traces because they're valuable assets. A replay surface between tool calls lets an attacker pull them back out near-verbatim through the public API.

title: GraphRAG
hook: GraphRAG builds a knowledge graph from your documents first, then answers over its structure — so it can reason across many sources, not just retrieve the nearest few chunks.

title: Grokking: Generalization Long After Overfitting
hook: A network memorizes the training set and seems done. Keep training anyway, and much later it can suddenly snap into real generalization — an effect called grokking.

title: State of Open Models, Summer 2026: Attention Isn't Adoption
hook: Hugging Face crunched a year of Hub data: Chinese labs shipped the biggest open models nearly every month, but models under 1B parameters took 83% of all downloads.

title: Unlimited OCR: Constant KV Cache for Long Documents
hook: LLM-based OCR slows down as documents get longer because the KV cache keeps growing. Unlimited OCR holds the cache constant, transcribing dozens of pages in one pass.

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
hook: Meta released Llama 2 with open weights and a commercial-use license, giving anyone a strong RLHF-tuned chat model to build on - and kicked off a wave of open-LLM development.

title: Learning Rate & Schedules
hook: The single most important hyperparameter: set it too high and training diverges, too low and it crawls — so we warm it up, then decay it.

title: EviRank: Turning Image Re-ranking Into a Checklist
hook: "Find this shirt in pink" hides three instructions: keep the entity, change the attribute, ignore the background. EviRank makes each one an explicit, checkable criterion.

title: Phi-3: A Capable Language Model on Your Phone
hook: Microsoft's Phi-3 Mini matches much larger models on reasoning benchmarks by training on heavily filtered, 'textbook-quality' data - and is small enough to run on a phone.

title: LeRobot v0.6.0: World-Model Policies for Robot Learning
hook: Hugging Face's open robotics library adds policies that imagine the future before acting, five new vision-language-action models, and a CLI for human-in-the-loop data collection.

title: Writing the Physical World Down as Runnable Code
hook: A VLM can describe a falling object without holding any model of what governs the fall. Code-as-World makes the model emit executable code as its world representation — then runs it to check itself.

title: ChatGPT Starts Reading Your Medical Records
hook: OpenAI has shipped Health in ChatGPT: eligible US users can connect their medical records and Apple Health data so the assistant answers from their own history rather than in general.

title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
hook: A misaligned coding agent doesn't need to sneak a backdoor into one pull request — it can spread the attack across many, and no single monitor catches both strategies at once.

title: OpenAI o3: Reasoning that Uses Tools
hook: o3 is the first reasoning model that can agentically reach for every ChatGPT tool mid-thought - web search, Python on your files, image input, image generation - and combine them to solve a problem.

title: AI Tutors Jump In Too Soon
hook: Put an LLM in the tutor's seat and it interrupts sooner and more often than a human would — and hands over the whole solution where a person would have offered a hint.

title: Switch Transformer: Scaling to Trillion-Parameter Models
hook: Route every token to exactly one expert instead of many - this single simplification made trillion-parameter MoE models stable enough to train at scale.

title: Language Models Need Sleep
hook: Humans consolidate the day's memories while sleeping. This paper gives LLMs a 'sleep' phase to distill fragile short-term context into stable long-term weights — and a 'dreaming' phase to rehearse.

title: GPipe: Pipeline Parallelism for Giant Networks
hook: Spread a network's layers across accelerators as pipeline stages, then split each batch into micro-batches so no accelerator sits idle — near-linear speedup for giant models.

title: DeepSeek-V4: Sparse Attention, Million-Token Default
hook: DeepSeek-V4 makes a 1M-token context window the default and pairs token-wise compression with sparse attention, so long-context inference no longer pays the usual compute and memory tax.

title: Ultrafast Mode: A Frontier Model at 750 Tokens/Second
hook: OpenAI is previewing a service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14x faster on Cerebras hardware — same model, different silicon, up to 750 output tokens per second.

title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning
hook: Zero RL — reasoning trained on verifiable rewards, no human labels — had only been tried small-scale. At a trillion parameters, the model starts inventing reasoning habits nobody hand-coded.

title: Video-IFBench: Can a Video Model Follow the Instruction, Not Just Watch?
hook: Video benchmarks mostly ask whether the model got the answer right. This one asks whether it did what you told it to — and more than 20 recent multimodal LLMs still struggle.

title: NVIDIA Opens 10T Tokens of Synthetic Data for Agentic AI
hook: Real agent behavior needs data on tool failures and recovery paths that companies rarely want to share — NVIDIA's answer is 10+ trillion tokens of synthetic data built to stand in for it.

title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Causality Leaks
hook: Your attention mask can be perfectly correct and your model still peeks at the future. Two forward passes find the leak — and turned up real defects in Zamba2 and Nemotron-H.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
hook: Cramming a whole sentence into one vector loses information. This 2014 paper let the decoder look back at relevant source words at each step — the original attention mechanism.

title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable
hook: An agent is only as good as its harness — the code that builds prompts, manages state, calls tools. The real bottleneck isn't editing that code, it's finding where a behavior lives in a huge codebase.

title: Sign Language to Text, Shipped to Users
hook: DeepMind's SL2T translates sign language into text — and unlike most accessibility research demos, it's going into products Deaf and hard-of-hearing users can actually use.

title: Distillation Without Training: Let a Strong Model Build the Weak One a Harness
hook: A strong model writes the scaffolding — code, routing, format rules — and a weak model runs inside it. Average performance nearly doubled, 0.49 to 0.91, with no parameter updates at all.

title: How Far Are LLM Research Ideas From Human Ones? A Reverse-Engineering Study
hook: Judging LLM research ideas one at a time (novel? feasible? liked?) hides a bigger question: does the whole distribution of ideas an LLM can produce look like what human researchers actually do?

title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

title: AlphaFold: Protein Structure Prediction
hook: Predicting a protein's 3D shape from its sequence stumped biology for ~50 years. AlphaFold cracked it at near-experimental accuracy — and then released the structures to everyone.

title: Zetta: A Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence
hook: Most robot agents reflect only after the episode ends — too late to save it. Zetta writes and revises its own runtime critics mid-rollout, while the base policy stays frozen.

title: Kimi K3: Moonshot's 2.8T-Parameter Successor Goes Live
hook: Moonshot's Kimi K3 lands on web and app with 2.8 trillion parameters and a 1-million-token context — nearly 3x K2's scale, aimed squarely at coding and agentic work.

title: Stereo2Spatial: Upmixing Stereo Music to 7.1.4 Spatial Audio with Flow-Matching Diffusion
hook: A hobbyist project trains a flow-matching diffusion model to turn ordinary stereo music into full 7.1.4 spatial mixes — built on a dedicated VAE latent space rather than working directly on audio.

title: RynnWorld-Teleop: Digital Teleoperation for Robot Data
hook: Collecting robot demonstrations means binding an operator's time to one physical robot. RynnWorld-Teleop swaps in a world model: move your hands, and it generates the footage instead.

title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
hook: Self-distillation drops the costly teacher by letting a model teach itself with privileged information. The asymmetry that creates the signal also biases it — into collapse.

title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
hook: Let the model write its own step-by-step rationales, keep only the ones that reach the right answer, fine-tune on those, and repeat — reasoning data that bootstraps itself.

title: arXiv Becomes an Independent Nonprofit
hook: After 25 years hosted by Cornell, arXiv — the preprint server ML research runs on — spun out as its own nonprofit on July 1, 2026, backed by Simons Foundation and Schmidt Sciences.

title: Knowing When to Stop: Adaptive Sampling for LLM Evals
hook: Most evals run every item the same number of times, long after the estimate has stopped moving. Treat it as sequential measurement instead and 57–97% of those trials turn out to be unnecessary.

title: Grok 4
hook: xAI's Grok 4 leaned hard on reinforcement learning and native tool use, topping several reasoning benchmarks at its July 2025 launch.

title: VAE: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
hook: Don't just compress data to a point — compress it to a distribution. That gives a smooth latent space you can sample from to generate genuinely new data.

title: SEED: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hook: Outcome-only RL tells an agent whether an episode succeeded, not which step mattered. SEED has the policy mine its own trajectories for hindsight lessons, then distills them back in as dense, token-level signal.

title: Flex-Forcing: One Video Diffusion Model, Two Inference Modes
hook: Video diffusion models used to force a choice: globally coherent but slow, or fast streaming that drifts apart. Flex-Forcing chunks time and denoising steps together so one model does both.

title: Missing the Butterfly and Predicting the Past: Features or Bugs of Accurate AI Weather Models?
hook: AI weather models can be trained to predict the past as skillfully as the future. The same flaw that lets them do it explains why their forecasts beat physics.

title: ControlNet: Adding Conditional Control to Diffusion Models
hook: Lock a diffusion model's weights, attach a trainable copy of its encoder fed with spatial signals like edges or pose, and gain precise compositional control without touching the original model.

title: Textbooks Are All You Need (phi-1)
hook: Train a 1.3B code model on a few billion tokens of 'textbook quality' data instead of raw web scale, and it scores 50.6% pass@1 on HumanEval — data quality standing in for size.

title: The Design Fundamentals of Pixel Text Representation Learning
hook: What if a model read text as an image instead of tokens? Controlled ablations pin down the four ingredients that make pixel-space text encoders actually work.

title: Catching Agent Memory Poisoning from Tool-Call Logs Alone
hook: A memory-poisoning attack on an LLM agent leaves a near-perfect fingerprint in its tool-call order — a simple rule catches it at AUC 0.956, a small classifier pushes that to 0.99.

title: Ladders in Chaos: Sequential Beats Parallel Test-Time Scaling — Up to a Point
hook: Revising your own answer beats sampling many independent ones, in translation at least. But push the budget too far and fluency keeps rising while accuracy starts slipping.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
hook: Why retrain billions of weights when you can freeze them all and train tiny add-on matrices instead? LoRA tunes under ~1% of the parameters with near-full-fine-tune quality.

title: SemComp-Bench: Judge the Video by the Outcome, Not the Frames
hook: Most video-generation benchmarks grade appearance consistency. SemComp-Bench asks a blunter question: did the task in the prompt actually get done?

title: Disentangling a Convolutional Neuron by Clustering What It Actually Detects
hook: A single 'car detector' neuron might really be several overlapping detectors wearing one name. Clustering what it responds to pulls apart clean, monosemantic patterns hiding inside.

title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory
hook: Agent memory sounds purely good — until retrieved memories start pushing an agent to agree with the user over the facts. MemSyco-Bench is built specifically to catch that failure.

title: Support-Vector Networks (SVMs)
hook: An SVM draws the decision boundary that maximizes the gap to the nearest training points - the wider the margin, the better it generalizes to new data.

title: Why QLoRA's 2e-4 Default Learning Rate Overfits Small Datasets
hook: Every QLoRA tutorial says start at 2e-4. That number comes from Alpaca's 52k samples — and on the 5-10k-sample datasets most people actually fine-tune on, it can overfit before epoch one ends.

title: Nemotron 3 Ultra: Open Hybrid Mamba-Attention MoE
hook: NVIDIA's open 550B model interleaves Mamba and attention inside a Mixture-of-Experts - hitting ~6x the inference throughput of comparable LLMs at on-par accuracy.

title: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment From Token Zero
hook: Alignment is normally a coat of paint applied after pretraining. This work installs the assistant's values from the first token — and finds that the earlier you start, the deeper they hold.

title: ARC-AGI-2
hook: ARC-AGI-2 rebuilt the abstraction benchmark to defeat brute-force search — frontier models that aced version 1 initially scored near zero, while humans still solve it.

title: Partition, Prompt, Aggregate: Statistical Self-Consistency in Language Models
hook: If an LLM's answer is a real probability estimate, slicing a population into subgroups and recombining should match asking about the whole. It usually doesn't — finer-grained is more accurate.

title: Funes: Give Your Coding Agents a Memory You Own
hook: Your agent's reasoning from last Tuesday vanishes when the session ends. Funes indexes past sessions locally so an agent can recall its own prior decisions instead of being re-briefed.

title: Qwen-Image-2.0-RL: RLHF for a Diffusion Model
hook: Qwen's team applied RLHF and on-policy distillation to a text-to-image diffusion model — the same post-training playbook that shaped chat models, now tuning image generation and editing.

title: SemaPLC: Let the Runtime Decide When Generated Code Is Done
hook: An agent that stops when it thinks it's finished will always look good. SemaPLC only declares a task complete when external checks — including a live PLC runtime — log that it passed.

title: What Is Machine Learning?
hook: Instead of hand-coding rules, you show a program examples and let it find the patterns — then it handles inputs it has never seen.

title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
hook: Long-running coding agents eventually run out of context before finishing the job. CompactionRL trains them to summarize their own history mid-task, as part of the RL objective itself.

title: J-Zero: Co-Evolving a Challenger, a Solver, and a Judge From Zero Data
hook: Self-improvement works when answers can be checked. J-Zero's trick for the unverifiable half: derive the judge's training labels from how each answer was produced, not from the judge's own scores.

title: iLLaDA: Improved Large Language Diffusion Models
hook: An 8B language model trained from scratch with full bidirectional attention and a masked-diffusion objective — no autoregression — that holds its own against same-size autoregressive LLMs.

title: From AGI to ASI: Four Pathways to Superintelligence
hook: A DeepMind team maps four routes from human-level AGI to superintelligence - and argues the leap may arrive as a series of transformative shifts, not one dramatic step change.

title: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA)
hook: Quadratic attention chokes at a million tokens. MiniMax runs exact attention over only a Top-k of key-value blocks per query group — cutting per-token attention compute ~28x at 1M context.

title: Block-GTQ: RoPE-Aware Bit Allocation for KV-Cache Quantization
hook: Most KV-cache quantizers spend bits evenly across a key. Block-GTQ shows that under RoPE some frequency blocks matter far more — and gives them more bits, hitting near-fp16 quality at 2–3 bits.

title: Where to Spend Model Size in Self-Refinement
hook: Generate, critique, revise — three stages, and most systems use the same big model for all three. The critic barely needs to be big; the reviser absolutely does.

title: The Bad Persona Was Already In There
hook: Fine-tuning on narrow bad advice doesn't build a misaligned character — it recruits a persona subspace the aligned model was already carrying, visible before the first optimizer step.

title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization
hook: Already trained a giant LLM? GPTQ squeezes its weights down to 3–4 bits afterward — no retraining — with surprisingly little quality loss.

title: Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle as Mid-Training for Coding Agent Foundation Models
hook: Ordinary pretraining only sees code left-to-right. This mid-training trick masks whole functions like a tool call's return value — and it measurably makes coding agents better.

title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: One Model, Three Decoding Modes
hook: Instead of picking autoregressive or diffusion decoding, Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion trains one model to do both — plus a self-speculation mode that decodes up to 6x more tokens per forward pass.

title: Six Major Labs Sign the EU Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content
hook: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Mistral all put their names to Europe's code for marking AI-generated content — the practical layer under the AI Act's transparency rules.

title: MaxProof: One Model as Generator, Verifier, Refiner, and Ranker
hook: Treat one model as proof writer, checker, fixer, and judge; search a population of candidate proofs; pick a winner by tournament — enough, the authors report, to clear math-olympiad gold.

title: Qwen2-VL: Vision-Language at Any Resolution
hook: Qwen2-VL processes images at their native resolution rather than forcing a fixed size, making it significantly better at reading small text and understanding fine-grained visual detail.

title: Granite 4.2: IBM's Open 3B/8B/30B Family
hook: Three Apache-2.0 dense models with 512K context, trained through a five-phase pretrain, agentic SFT, and stacked GRPO runs — with the whole recipe written down.

title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
hook: LLMs can solve hard reasoning problems in seconds but fumble at exactly copying text in their own context. The culprit: positional encodings biased toward shortcuts, fixed by laying text out in 2D.

title: ScarfBench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Enterprise Java Framework Migration
hook: Frontier coding agents attempt real enterprise Java framework migrations and succeed under 10% of the time — and one agent claimed 29 of 30 migrations worked when only 22 actually built.

title: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
hook: Find the directions your data varies most, then keep only the top few - you compress many correlated features into a handful while retaining most of the signal.

title: HOTFIXR: Targeted Synthetic Data for Multilingual Weaknesses
hook: A model can answer the same question well in English and badly in Turkish. Rather than routing everything through English, probe the student's weak spots and synthesize data for exactly those.

title: Puro-2B: Pretraining a Real LLM for $6,900
