hook: Reproducing SmolLM3-3B costs over $700K. This team pretrained a 2B model on 1.4T tokens using consumer RTX 5090s for under $6.9K — and released the whole recipe.

title: Doomed from the Start: Predicting Agent Failure Before It Happens
hook: An agent that's going to fail often shows it in its hidden activations from round one — long before its actual behavior looks any different. Reading that signal saves nearly half the compute.

title: ToolHazard: Synthesizing Adversarial Environments for Agent Security
hook: Prompt-injection benchmarks are hand-built, so they cover the domains someone had time to write. ToolHazard generates the environments — and the attacks inside them — instead.

title: Learning Words Like a Child
hook: Most models learn from data shuffled and replayed for hundreds of epochs. BabyCL learns word-object links from a child's-eye video in one pass through time — close to how a kid actually learns.

title: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel While an Agent Acts
hook: Every time a ReAct agent calls a tool and waits, its reasoning sits idle. Second Thought fills that gap with side branches that think ahead — no retraining, fewer turns.

title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
hook: RLHF works but is fiddly: a separate reward model and a finicky RL loop. DPO reaches the same goal with one simple loss — and became a popular default.

title: Classifier-Free Guidance
hook: Want a diffusion model to follow your prompt more closely? Blend its prompt-aware and prompt-blind predictions — no extra classifier required. That's the guidance-scale slider.

title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open-Source Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
hook: An open recipe for text-to-image, editing, and bilingual text rendering that closes in on closed-source giants — for a reported $400K training budget.

title: Gemini 3.7 Flash: The Workhorse Gets Agentic
hook: Google's cheap-and-fast tier now targets long-horizon engineering work — DeepSWE jumps from 49.0% to 65.3% over 3.6 Flash, at $0.75 per million input tokens.

title: IDEAgent: Quality-Diversity Search for Research Ideas
hook: Idea generators optimize for quality or for diversity, and get either near-clones or piles of nonsense. Treating ideation as a joint search changes the objective.

title: Multi-Vector Retrieval: One Vector Per Token, Scored Late
hook: Squeezing a document into one vector throws away where the match was. Late interaction keeps a vector per token and defers scoring — better recall, 42x the index.

title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
hook: On-device models ship small vocabularies to save memory, so languages added later get shredded into extra tokens. This recipe grows the tokenizer after the fact — no retraining from scratch.

title: Scaling Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning with NVIDIA NeMo Automodel and Hugging Face Diffusers
hook: Fine-tuning video and image diffusion models usually means outgrowing single-GPU Diffusers scripts fast. NVIDIA's NeMo Automodel now plugs into Diffusers to take that fine-tuning to multi-GPU scale.

title: Reading Between the Dots: Hidden Computation in Filler Tokens
hook: Frontier models can solve multi-step problems while outputting nothing but dots — no visible reasoning at all. This paper shows that 'hidden' computation is still legible, just not in the output.

title: xHC: Expanded Hyper-Connections
hook: Hyper-Connections let a transformer keep several parallel residual streams instead of one — a big win from 1 to 4 streams, then a wall. xHC breaks the wall, scaling cleanly to 16 on real MoE models.

title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
hook: Robot policies mostly look at the last step or two. NVIDIA's RoboTTT pushes visuomotor context to 8,000 timesteps without slowing inference — and finds performance keeps climbing the whole way.

title: SANA-Video 2.0: Softmax Where It Counts
hook: Pure linear attention is cheap but loses full-rank token mixing. SANA-Video 2.0 sprinkles softmax anchors back in at a 3:1 ratio and reaches softmax-level video quality at linear-attention cost.

title: Gated Recurrent Transformers: Buying Depth with Recurrence
hook: Sharing one transformer block across many layers saves memory but flattens the model. Add a GRU-style update gate and the same three layers can act like twelve.

title: k-Means Clustering
hook: Pick k cluster centers, assign every point to the nearest one, move each center to the mean of its points, repeat - clusters emerge without any labels.

title: SciReasoner: Native Structural Reasoning Across Proteins, Molecules, and Crystals
hook: Most scientific AI predicts an answer without showing its structural work. SciReasoner turns 3D structure itself into evidence tokens the model reasons over — and hits SOTA on 67 of 86 benchmarks.

title: TorchJD: Stop Averaging Your Losses, Aggregate Their Gradients
hook: Multi-task training usually blends losses into one number before taking a gradient step. TorchJD instead keeps every loss's own gradient and combines them so each one actually goes down.

title: Task Crossover: AI Is Redrawing Who Does What at Work
hook: In 800,000+ ChatGPT messages, 43.5% of occupation-specific work use involves tasks from another job. AI is redrawing job boundaries before the job titles catch up.

title: Three Ways to Fuse Domain Experts, Compared
hook: Merge task vectors, pool the RL data, or distil from multiple teachers? Average scores differ by 1.4 points — but on a single benchmark the gap hits 8.6.

title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Choosing Is the Bottleneck, Not Generating
hook: Spend more inference compute on open-ended tasks and the best candidate in your pool keeps getting better. The problem is you can't tell which one it is.

title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
hook: Run a frozen, untrained model through your self-improvement pipeline and it appears to gain and lose capabilities. Without that control, seven common measurement habits invert their own findings.

title: How Neural Networks Learn: Backpropagation
hook: A neural net learns by asking, for every weight, 'how much did you contribute to my mistake?' Backprop answers all of them at once.

title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models
hook: Treat a robot's actions as just more text tokens, and a vision-language model can learn to act — carrying its web knowledge into the physical world.

title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion for High-Resolution Synthesis
hook: A larger UNet, two text encoders, and a refinement diffusion stage gave open-source Stable Diffusion a major quality leap - now the workhorse of community image generation.

title: Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability?
hook: An agent score only means something if the task still requires the skill it claims to test. Auditing 2,385 traces, two-thirds showed the agent taking a shortcut instead.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
hook: DeepSeek-V3 trained a frontier-class MoE model for a fraction of the cost of comparable closed models, using FP8 training and a novel load-balancing scheme to make efficiency the headline result.

title: A Complete Text-to-Speech Stack in 16 MB
hook: Text in, 24 kHz speech out — no external vocoder, no hosted API. Inflect v2's smaller model is 3.96M parameters total, counting every stage of the pipeline.

title: Batch Normalization
hook: Re-center and re-scale each layer's activations on every minibatch, and deep nets suddenly train faster and tolerate much higher learning rates.

title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs
hook: Speculative decoding assumes drafter and verifier read the same context. Let the small drafter see everything while the big model reads a compressed view, and compression stops costing accuracy.

title: Muse Glimmer: Meta's 30B Local Agentic Multimodal Model
hook: Meta distilled its Muse model down to 30B and shipped it Apache 2.0 — a vision-and-text model built to run locally and call tools, not just chat.

title: Post-Training Shifts Confidence: SFT, RL, and OPD Shape Calibration Differently
hook: SFT, RL, and on-policy distillation all boost reasoning accuracy — but they leave completely different fingerprints on when a model's confidence signal can actually be trusted.

title: Use a Weak Model to Stop Your Strong One Getting Stuck
hook: RLVR collapses a model's entropy until it only knows one way to think. Feeding it half-finished reasoning from a smaller, worse model breaks the rut — no reward engineering required.

title: Pushing the Frontier of Full-Song Generation
hook: Full, multi-minute songs from just lyrics and a text prompt: a two-stage system plans the song autoregressively, then renders it with flow matching for high-fidelity audio.

title: GPT-5.6: Frontier Intelligence That Scales With Your Ambition
hook: GPT-5.6 ships as three tiers instead of one model — Luna, Terra, Sol — built around squeezing more capability out of every token rather than just scaling up.

title: The Loss Doesn't See the Basis, But Adam Does
hook: A factored model's loss can't tell which basis you wrote the factors in — but Adam's per-coordinate scaling can. That asymmetry predicts which optimizers keep gradient descent's low-rank bias.

title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
hook: When software is part of the scientific instrument, a bad patch corrupts the evidence. The best agent tested clears under 50% of these repo-level scientific fixes.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): A Standard for Connecting LLMs to Tools
hook: MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications expose tools, data, and resources to models - think USB-C for AI tool integrations.

title: SAE Interventions Are Unreliable
hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.

title: CLAP: One World Model, Many Bodies
hook: Action-conditioned video models are usually locked to one robot, which locks them out of internet video. CLAP unifies action spaces so human footage and robot logs can train the same world model.

title: EdgeBench: Scaling Laws for Learning from Real Environments
hook: Pretraining has scaling laws everyone knows by heart. This paper finds the first one for what happens after deployment — how fast agents actually improve from real-world experience.

title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
hook: Rule-based data cleaning is too rigid; LLM rewrites are too slow at pretraining scale. UltraX teaches a model to emit structured, executable edit programs instead — insertions included.

title: Debias-SparseGPT: Pruning a Model Can Amplify Its Biases
hook: Compression isn't neutral. Weight sparsification has been shown to amplify existing bias, with outputs swinging on persona cues — so this method adds a debiasing term to the pruning objective itself.

title: Adversarial Attacks for Good: Turning Perturbations into Owner-Side Protection
hook: The perturbations that fool vision models can be applied by the content's owner instead — to block recognition, poison scrapers, or break unauthorized edits. Five communities invented this separately.

title: A Hobbyist CUDA Kernel Brings DeepSeek-V4 Flash's Full 1M Context to One GPU
hook: Missing CUDA support for DeepSeek-V4 Flash's sparse-attention indexer meant llama.cpp needed ~256GB of VRAM for 1M-token context. One contributor's kernel patch shrinks that to a single RTX 5090.

title: Adam: The Default Optimizer
hook: Adam gives every parameter its own adaptive step size by tracking the gradient's recent average and spread — and it mostly just works.

title: Hugging Face and Cerebras Bring Gemma 4 to Real-Time Voice AI
hook: Multi-second delays are why voice assistants feel like phone menus. Running Gemma 4 on Cerebras hardware in a modular speech pipeline already powers 9,000+ Reachy Mini robots in production.

title: Grok Build CLI Uploads Your Whole Repo, No Matter What You Tell It
hook: A researcher wire-tapped xAI's coding CLI and found it uploads your entire repo - full git history and .env secrets - no matter what you tell it not to touch.

title: Self-Instruct: Aligning LMs with Self-Generated Instructions
hook: Instead of paying humans to write instruction data, have the model write its own — bootstrap instructions, inputs, and outputs from its own generations, filter, and fine-tune.

title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal
hook: Safety pipelines suppress eval-awareness as if it were one quantity. It isn't: reading a test as a capability check rather than a boundary probe swings compliance by up to 46 points.

title: S4: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
hook: A clever matrix parameterization turns the notoriously unstable state-space recurrence into a stable, fast sequence model that handles sequences 100x longer than Transformers.

title: Deep Residual Learning (ResNet)
hook: Stacking more layers used to make networks worse, not better. ResNet's fix — let each layer learn a tweak to its input — unlocked nets over 100 layers deep.

title: WILDTRACE: Benchmarking Natural Evidence Trails in Long-Context Reasoning
hook: Most long-context tests plant a fake 'needle' in a haystack. Real evidence doesn't look like that — passing needle tests may not mean a model can truly reason over a document.

title: Extending Context Windows via Positional Interpolation
hook: Don't extrapolate to positions the model never saw - squeeze the position indices back inside the trained range, and a short fine-tune stretches the context window many times over.

title: Multimodal Reward Hacking: RL Creates It, Doesn't Just Inherit It
hook: Train a multimodal model with outcome-only RL rewards and it doesn't just exploit shortcuts it already had — the training itself manufactures new ones, up to 48% of the time.

title: UMAP's Forgotten Graph: Network Science for Free Sensemaking
hook: Everyone uses UMAP for its 2D scatter plot and throws away the graph it builds along the way — a graph that's still faithful to the data manifold, and worth analyzing on its own.

title: Segment Anything (SAM)
hook: Click a point or drag a box, and it instantly masks the object — even in images it has never seen. SAM is a foundation model for segmentation.

title: KV Cache Eviction, Formalized
hook: Everyone drops KV cache entries with clever heuristics. Formalize the problem properly and it turns into expectation estimation — which finally lets you correct for what you threw away.

title: Separating Signal from Noise in Coding Evaluations
hook: OpenAI told the field to switch to SWE-Bench Pro after finding SWE-bench Verified contaminated. Now its own audit says ~30% of SWE-Bench Pro's tasks are broken too.

title: On the Measure of Intelligence (ARC)
hook: Is a high benchmark score the same as intelligence? Chollet argues no — intelligence is how efficiently you acquire new skills, not how well you perform known ones.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
hook: Meta's Llama 3 family, trained on roughly 15 trillion tokens with a 405B-parameter flagship, narrowed the gap to closed frontier models while staying open-weights.

title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
hook: A2A is an open standard for agents from different vendors to discover and delegate to each other — the agent-to-agent complement to MCP's agent-to-tool layer.

title: Critique of Agent Model: Agentic vs. Agentive Systems
hook: When is a system really an 'agent' and not just a clever workflow? This paper draws the line at whether agency is internalized or scaffolded — and sketches an architecture for the former.

title: Mistral Medium 3
hook: Mistral Medium 3 chased frontier-class quality at a fraction of the cost — 'medium is the new large' — aimed squarely at enterprise deployment.

title: Agents' Last Exam: Benchmarking Agents on Real Economic Work
hook: Frontier agents ace academic benchmarks but flop on real jobs — Agents' Last Exam scores them on 1,000+ economically valuable workflows, where the hardest tier sees just a 2.6% pass rate.

title: Skill Issue: Are Skills Language-Invariant in LLMs?
hook: Have a model play a game against itself, one copy in English and one in another language. Same model, same rules, same board — and markedly different playing strength.

title: The Annotated Transformer
hook: Want to truly get multi-head attention? Read the Transformer paper line by line — next to runnable PyTorch that implements every equation.

title: WeatherNext Cyclones: An Extra Day of Hurricane Warning
hook: DeepMind's cyclone model makes three-day forecasts as accurate as yesterday's two-day forecasts — about a decade of meteorological progress, delivered in under a minute on a TPU.

title: How Rhetoric Reward-Hacks an AI Reviewer
hook: Rewrite a paper's framing without changing a single result, and LLM reviewers move their scores. The effect is structured: evidence framing and novelty stance move them most.

title: Gemma 4 QAT: 4-Bit Weights That Keep Their Quality
hook: Squeezing a model to 4 bits after training loses quality. Quantization-aware training bakes the rounding into training instead — and Google shipped Gemma 4 checkpoints that do exactly that.

title: PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation
hook: Full agentic evals like SWE-Bench and GAIA can cost thousands of dollars and days to run — PACE predicts those scores from a tiny, cheap subset of ordinary benchmarks, at under 1% of the cost.

title: GLM-5.2
hook: z.ai's GLM-5.2 became the strongest open-weights model of mid-2026 — the first reported to clear 80% on Terminal-Bench and a coding favorite that rivals top closed models at a fraction of the cost.

title: GSM8K: Training Verifiers for Grade-School Math
hook: Instead of trusting a model's first answer, sample many and let a learned 'verifier' pick the best — and it beats just finetuning, scaling better with data.

title: Sora 2
hook: OpenAI's Sora 2 added synchronized audio and sharper physical consistency — and shipped inside a TikTok-style social app where you remix each other's generations.

title: On-Policy Delta Distillation
hook: Instead of copying a teacher's raw outputs, this method distills only the *change* reasoning-tuning made — a sharper signal that beats standard on-policy distillation across math, science, and code.

title: Economy of Minds: Agents That Bid to Act
hook: Skip the orchestrator. Let agents bid in auctions for the right to act, pay each other, and accumulate wealth — and collective intelligence emerges from the market, not from central control.

title: GPT-4o: One Model for Text, Audio, and Vision
hook: GPT-4o is a single model that natively processes text, audio, and images end-to-end - no separate speech pipeline - cutting voice response latency to near human conversational speed.

title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro Ships for Real: 1.7T Under MIT
hook: The preview is over. DeepSeek's 1.7-trillion-parameter MoE lands with open MIT weights, built-in speculative decoding, and benchmark claims aimed straight at the closed frontier.

title: PagedAttention / vLLM: Efficient LLM Serving
hook: LLM serving wastes huge amounts of GPU memory on the attention cache. PagedAttention borrows an OS trick — paging — to recover it and serve many more requests at once.

title: What an Engram Actually Is
hook: The n-gram tables in new open models are not a trick for running 1T parameters off an SSD — they are an embedding table with a longer key, and that is a more interesting idea.

title: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large MoEs
hook: Sweeping learning rates at trillion-token scale is unaffordable. Transfer across width with muP, then extrapolate along tokens with a fitted scaling law — and trust it for the real run.

title: Piloting the World's First Double-Blind AI Evaluations
hook: Benchmarks only mean something if the model hasn't seen the answers. DeepMind's pilot hides the test from the lab and the weights from the evaluators — enforced by cryptography, not a contract.

title: Ring Forcing: Teaching Video Models Object Permanence
hook: Long video generation breaks in two ways at once: models forget what an object looked like, and can't reach far enough back to check. Ring Forcing attacks both.

title: AlphaZero: Mastering Games from Scratch
hook: AlphaGo learned from human games. AlphaZero threw those away — one algorithm reached superhuman chess, shogi, and Go knowing only the rules and playing itself.

title: How Language Models Organize Moral Knowledge
hook: Six moral foundations, six linear probes: the directions neither collapse into one 'morality detector' nor sit independently — they span near-maximal dimensions while sharing a common component.

title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Test-Time Compute
hook: Let the model pick its own thinking budget with its very first token. On MATH500 that cut response length 41% while accuracy barely moved.

title: AI Watermark Evidence Fails Forensic Readiness
hook: Laws like the EU AI Act and California's SB 942 assume watermark detection can hold up in court. Tested against forensic and legal admissibility standards, three leading methods collapse.

title: Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories
hook: A 3,843-trajectory autopsy of coding agents finds most failures aren't slips — they're wrong beliefs formed in the first few steps, invisible until it's too late to recover.

title: Trace: A Taxonomy-Guided Environment for Multidomain Visual Reasoning
hook: Verifiable-reward training sharpened text reasoning but stalls on vision — exact-answer image tasks are hard to make at scale. Trace generates them procedurally, and it transfers to real benchmarks.

title: Muon: An Optimizer for Hidden Layers
hook: Muon orthogonalizes each gradient update before applying it — and trained networks faster than AdamW, the first serious challenger to Adam's reign in years.

title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
hook: LLM judge bias isn't just noisy scoring — it has a geometric signature in hidden states you can find, steer, and use to predict failures on benchmarks you've never tested.

title: Hugging Face Discloses a Security Incident Driven End-to-End by an AI Agent
hook: Hugging Face says it caught and contained a production intrusion carried out entirely by an autonomous AI agent — detected largely by its own AI-based anomaly triage, not a human tip.

title: UI-MOPD: Teaching One GUI Agent Many Platforms Without Forgetting
hook: Train a GUI agent on a new platform and it often forgets the old ones. UI-MOPD picks a different teacher per platform on the fly, so cross-platform learning stops fighting itself.

title: DocOps: Benchmarking Agents That Edit Real Documents
hook: Even frontier agents can't reliably edit complex documents: a verifiable benchmark pins the failures on three modes — state-tracking collapse, shallow verification, and destructive metadata edits.

title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: Verification as a New Scaling Axis
hook: Everyone scales pretraining, post-training, and test-time compute. This paper argues verification — checking if a solution is correct — is its own scaling axis, and hits SOTA on four agentic benchmarks.

title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
hook: A transformer uses one stream to both predict the next token and carry state for future predictions — split those two jobs apart, and the model gets measurably better.

title: Quantization-Aware Distillation: Train the 4-bit Model, Don't Squash It
hook: Liquid AI distilled BF16 teachers straight into Q4_0 students and recovered 97% of the accuracy that post-training quantization was throwing away.

title: What Are State-Space Models?
hook: A compact hidden state summarizes everything seen so far - update it with each new input and you get sequence modeling that scales linearly, not quadratically.

title: Growing Agent Training Tasks by Recursion, at Five Cents Each
hook: Hand-authored long-horizon agent tasks cost hundreds of dollars apiece. RST grows them recursively from verified seeds — 37,484 tasks at roughly $0.05 each, with no ceiling in sight.

title: A Formal Limit on What Any Model Can Learn From Text Alone
hook: There is a ceiling on how well meaning can be recovered from the form of an utterance — and it holds for any text representation, no matter how much data or supervision produced it.

title: SeededGrasp: Language-Guided Grasping in Complex Scenes with Multiple Embodiments
hook: Instead of one giant end-to-end model, let the VLM just point — predict a seed point, then hand off to a lightweight grasp generator. Data-efficient, and it transfers across robot hands.

title: Entity Binding Failures in Tool-Augmented Agents
hook: An agent can pick the right tool and still email the wrong Alex — 'entity binding' failures slip past standard tool-correctness checks in up to 26% of runs.

title: ActionCache: A Warm-Start Cache for Slow Robot Action Generation
hook: Flow-matching robot policies denoise every action from scratch, which is precise but slow. ActionCache lets a new action warm-start from a similar past one instead — no retraining, up to 34x faster.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep CNNs (AlexNet)
hook: In 2012 a single deep CNN trained on two GPUs crushed the ImageNet contest by a wide margin — and kicked off the deep learning era.

title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
hook: Self-distillation that finally deserves the name: no ground truth, no bigger teacher — just a model voting against itself and fixing where it was confidently wrong.

title: ABot-N1: Toward a General Visual Language Navigation Model
hook: Most navigation policies map pixels straight to actions and drift or guess blindly. ABot-N1 splits the job — reason slowly, point at a pixel, act fast — and posts new SOTA.

title: Route the Task, Not the Call
hook: Agent quality only reveals itself at the end of a long workflow — so a router deciding per LLM call can never tell which decision earned the reward. Decide once, at admission.

title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors
hook: The 1986 paper that made deep learning possible: run the error backward through the network with the chain rule, and you get every weight's gradient in one sweep.

title: OpenSkillRisk: Benchmarking Agent Safety with Risky Third-Party Skills
hook: Give an AI agent a third-party 'skill' and even the safest setups still run unsafe actions about 17% of the time — a benchmark of 263 risky skills shows exactly how they slip through.

title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face
hook: The default public home for open-weight models is being bought by the company that sells the chips to run them — reported at roughly $13 billion.

title: Humanoid-GPT: Scaling Data and Structure for Zero-Shot Motion Tracking
hook: What happens when you train whole-body humanoid control like a language model? A GPT-style transformer on 2 billion frames of motion that tracks new moves it never saw in training.

title: Xiaomi Quietly Ships MiMo-V2.5-DFlash
hook: Xiaomi quietly uploaded a speculative-decoding-style variant of its 300B+ MiMo-V2.5 model that could roughly double consumer-hardware throughput - once software catches up.

title: U-Net: Encoder–Decoder for Segmentation
hook: A U-shaped net that shrinks an image down to capture context, then rebuilds it pixel by pixel — with shortcuts that preserve fine detail. Now the workhorse inside diffusion models.

title: AtlasVLA: Giving a Robot Policy a Memory of Where It Is and What It Has Done
hook: A wrist camera forgets an object the moment it leaves frame. AtlasVLA keeps a persistent 3D map plus a record of task progress — and beats multi-view baselines with one camera.

title: Hourglass Reasoning: Context Isolation for Rigorous Induction
hook: Telling a model to state its inferred rule barely helps it self-refine. Forcing only a compressed rule — not the full trace — through a bottleneck nearly doubles a benchmark score.

title: How Much Is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length
hook: Before an LLM writes a single token of its answer, its hidden state already seems to know roughly how long the answer will be — and the estimate jumps when it restarts a draft.

title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
hook: Ask an image generator for a real but obscure or brand-new entity, and it'll confidently draw the wrong thing. A new benchmark shows how bad that gets — and how to teach it to search instead.

title: LeVJEPA: Video Pretraining Without the Asymmetry
hook: Drop the EMA target encoder, the stop-gradient, and the crippled predictor — a single encoder with a provably collapse-free loss matches V-JEPA 2 at up to 20x less compute.
